challenges.title: Survey the SQL vs NoSQL landscape and build an npm integration cheat-sheet for NestJS
challenges.description: This is a research / documentation challenge; NO runnable code is required. The goal: survey the market and consolidate the findings into a single Google Docs with 3 mandatory pieces: (1) a taxonomy of the most common SQL and NoSQL families with their core traits; (2) a decision table "data shape -> which DB -> why"; (3) a cheat-sheet of the npm packages / drivers / first-party integrations needed to plug each DB into a NestJS app. The doc must be deep enough that a junior dev can finish reading and know which DB to pick for which use case and what to npm i to get started.
challenges.requirements:
Submit a single ***Google Docs*** link (share `Anyone with link: Viewer`). The doc must contain the following sections, in order, each as a Heading 1:

**Section 1. SQL taxonomy** - list and briefly describe **>= 5 SQL systems**: `PostgreSQL`, `MySQL` / `MariaDB`, `SQL Server`, `SQLite`, `Oracle` (bonus: add `CockroachDB` or `YugabyteDB` for distributed SQL). For each system, provide **>= 4 bullets**: storage engine, signature use case, strengths, limitations.

**Section 2. NoSQL taxonomy** - split into **5 families**, each with >= 2 representative products:
- ***Document***: `MongoDB`, `Couchbase`, `Amazon DocumentDB`.
- ***Key-Value***: `Redis`, `Amazon DynamoDB` (KV + document), `Etcd`.
- ***Wide-column***: `Apache Cassandra`, `ScyllaDB`, `HBase`.
- ***Graph***: `Neo4j`, `ArangoDB`, `Amazon Neptune`.
- ***Search / Time-series***: `Elasticsearch` / `OpenSearch`, `InfluxDB`, `TimescaleDB` (TimescaleDB lives on top of Postgres - mention it as a SQL/NoSQL hybrid).

**Section 3. Decision table "data shape -> DB"** - a table with **>= 6 rows**, 4 columns: `Data/query characteristic` | `Real use case` | `Recommended DB` | `Reason (>= 1 sentence)`. Example: tight relational data + ACID -> `PostgreSQL` -> "needs constraints + multi-table joins"; constantly shifting schema -> `MongoDB`; realtime counter / leaderboard -> `Redis` ZSET; full-text search -> `Elasticsearch`; time-series metrics -> `InfluxDB`; friend-of-friend social graph -> `Neo4j`.

**Section 4. NestJS npm integration cheat-sheet** - a table with **>= 10 rows**, 4 columns: `DB / kind` | `ORM or Driver` | `npm package usable from NestJS (installable via `npm i ...`)` | `Docs link`. Coverage must include at minimum:
- `PostgreSQL` + TypeORM -> `@nestjs/typeorm`, `typeorm`, `pg`.
- `PostgreSQL` + Prisma -> `prisma`, `@prisma/client` (note wrapper modules like `nestjs-prisma`).
- `PostgreSQL` + Drizzle -> `drizzle-orm`, `drizzle-kit`, `pg`.
- `PostgreSQL` + MikroORM -> `@mikro-orm/nestjs`, `@mikro-orm/core`, `@mikro-orm/postgresql`.
- `MySQL` / `MariaDB` -> `@nestjs/typeorm`, `typeorm`, `mysql2`.
- `SQLite` (dev/test) -> `typeorm`, `better-sqlite3`.
- `MongoDB` + Mongoose -> `@nestjs/mongoose`, `mongoose`.
- `MongoDB` + TypeORM -> `typeorm`, `mongodb`.
- `Redis` (cache / queue) -> `@nestjs/cache-manager`, `cache-manager`, `cache-manager-ioredis-yet` (or `@nestjs-modules/ioredis`, `ioredis`).
- `Elasticsearch` -> `@nestjs/elasticsearch`, `@elastic/elasticsearch`.
- `DynamoDB` -> `@aws-sdk/client-dynamodb`, `@aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb` (optionally `nestjs-dynamoose`).
- `Neo4j` -> `nest-neo4j`, `neo4j-driver`.

The `npm package` column must list real, installable packages; you verify yourself with `npm view <name>`. Fake / made-up packages cost the full prompt.

**Section 5. 3 NestJS module config snippets** - paste exactly 3 `imports: [...]` snippets (not a full project), copied from official docs:
- `TypeOrmModule.forRoot({ type: 'postgres', ... })`.
- `MongooseModule.forRoot('mongodb://...')`.
- One of: `CacheModule.register({ store: redisStore, ... })`, `ElasticsearchModule.register({ node: ... })`, or a DynamoDB client (AWS SDK v3 manual wire-up).

**Section 6. References** - bullet list of **>= 6 links** to official docs: NestJS `/techniques/database`, TypeORM, Prisma, Mongoose, ioredis, Elasticsearch JS client (no Medium, personal blogs, or StackOverflow).

**Forbidden:**
- Copy/pasting a table from a blog with minor edits - reviewer will Google a random row and, if it matches, the corresponding prompt is zeroed.
- Listing non-existent packages like `@nestjs/mongodb`, `@nestjs/redis`, `@nestjs/prisma` (none of which exist as first-party packages at the time of this challenge) -> npm package prompt is failed.
- Vague one-liners such as "SQL is good for relations, NoSQL is good for scale" -> reason prompt fails.
challenges.prerequisites:
- Basic SQL (SELECT / JOIN / INSERT).
- Some hands-on experience with any single DB (MySQL / Postgres / Mongo).
- Comfortable reading docs on npmjs.com and verifying packages via `npm view <name> version`.

translations.value: Khảo sát landscape SQL vs NoSQL và bảng tra cứu npm package tích hợp vào NestJS

Đây là challenge dạng research / documentation, KHÔNG yêu cầu viết code chạy thật. Mục tiêu: học viên phải đi nghiên cứu và tổng hợp thành 1 tài liệu Google Docs đủ 3 phần: (1) phân loại các họ SQL và NoSQL phổ biến trên thị trường kèm đặc trưng cốt lõi; (2) bảng quyết định "shape dữ liệu -> chọn DB nào -> lý do"; (3) bảng tra cứu npm package / driver / integration chính thức để cắm từng loại DB vào 1 app NestJS. Tài liệu phải đủ sâu để 1 dev junior đọc xong biết chọn DB nào cho use case nào và gõ npm i cái gì để bắt đầu.

**Mục 1. Phân loại SQL** - liệt kê và mô tả ngắn ≥ **5 hệ SQL** thông dụng: `PostgreSQL`, `MySQL` / `MariaDB`, `SQL Server`, `SQLite`, `Oracle` (khuyến khích thêm `CockroachDB` hoặc `YugabyteDB` cho distributed SQL). Mỗi hệ có **≥ 4 bullet**: engine chính, use case tiêu biểu, điểm mạnh, hạn chế.

**Mục 2. Phân loại NoSQL** - chia theo **5 họ**, mỗi họ nêu ≥ 2 sản phẩm đại diện:
- ***Document***: `MongoDB`, `Couchbase`, `Amazon DocumentDB`.
- ***Key-Value***: `Redis`, `Amazon DynamoDB` (có thể coi là KV + document), `Etcd`.
- ***Wide-column***: `Apache Cassandra`, `ScyllaDB`, `HBase`.
- ***Graph***: `Neo4j`, `ArangoDB`, `Amazon Neptune`.
- ***Search / Time-series***: `Elasticsearch` / `OpenSearch`, `InfluxDB`, `TimescaleDB` (TimescaleDB nằm trên Postgres - nêu rõ lai SQL/NoSQL).

**Mục 4. Bảng tra cứu npm package tích hợp vào NestJS** - bảng ≥ **10 dòng**, mỗi dòng 4 cột: `DB / loại` | `ORM hoặc Driver` | `npm package chính thức dùng cho NestJS (gõ `npm i ...` được)` | `Link docs`. Yêu cầu cover tối thiểu:
- `PostgreSQL` + TypeORM -> `@nestjs/typeorm`, `typeorm`, `pg`.
- `PostgreSQL` + Prisma -> `prisma`, `@prisma/client` (ghi chú module wrapper như `nestjs-prisma`).
- `PostgreSQL` + Drizzle -> `drizzle-orm`, `drizzle-kit`, `pg`.
- `PostgreSQL` + MikroORM -> `@mikro-orm/nestjs`, `@mikro-orm/core`, `@mikro-orm/postgresql`.
- `MySQL` / `MariaDB` -> `@nestjs/typeorm`, `typeorm`, `mysql2`.
- `SQLite` (dev/test) -> `typeorm`, `better-sqlite3`.
- `MongoDB` + Mongoose -> `@nestjs/mongoose`, `mongoose`.
- `MongoDB` + TypeORM -> `typeorm`, `mongodb`.
- `Redis` (cache / queue) -> `@nestjs/cache-manager`, `cache-manager`, `cache-manager-ioredis-yet` (hoặc `@nestjs-modules/ioredis`, `ioredis`).
- `Elasticsearch` -> `@nestjs/elasticsearch`, `@elastic/elasticsearch`.
- `DynamoDB` -> `@aws-sdk/client-dynamodb`, `@aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb` (có thể thêm `nestjs-dynamoose`).
- `Neo4j` -> `nest-neo4j`, `neo4j-driver`.

Cột "npm package chính thức" phải là tên package có thật, cài được; học viên tự verify bằng `npm view <name>` (liệt kê package không tồn tại / fake -> trừ đủ điểm prompt đó).

**Mục 5. 3 ví dụ snippet cấu hình NestJS module** - paste đúng 3 snippet `imports: [...]` (không phải full project), chỉ cần copy từ docs chính thức:
- `TypeOrmModule.forRoot({ type: 'postgres', ... })`.
- `MongooseModule.forRoot('mongodb://...')`.
- 1 trong 3: `CacheModule.register({ store: redisStore, ... })` hoặc `ElasticsearchModule.register({ node: ... })` hoặc `DynamoDBModule` (AWS SDK v3 manual).

**Mục 6. Tham chiếu (References)** - danh sách ≥ **6 link** đến docs chính thức: NestJS `/techniques/database`, TypeORM, Prisma, Mongoose, ioredis, Elasticsearch JS client (không tính link Medium, blog cá nhân, StackOverflow).

**Cấm:**
- Copy paste bảng từ 1 bài blog rồi đổi vài chữ - bị phát hiện (reviewer sẽ Google 1 dòng ngẫu nhiên trong bảng) -> **0 toàn prompt tương ứng**.
- Liệt kê package không tồn tại, ví dụ `@nestjs/mongodb` (không có), `@nestjs/redis` (không có chính thức), `@nestjs/prisma` (không có chính thức) -> trừ điểm prompt "npm package".
- Chỉ viết 1-2 dòng chung chung kiểu "SQL tốt cho quan hệ, NoSQL tốt cho scale" -> không đạt prompt lý do.

- Biết cơ bản cú pháp SQL (SELECT / JOIN / INSERT).
- Đã dùng qua ít nhất 1 DB bất kỳ (MySQL / Postgres / Mongo).
- Biết cách đọc docs trên npmjs.com và verify package tồn tại bằng `npm view <name> version`.

steps.title: Create an empty Google Doc and lay out the 6 required sections
steps.body:
**Steps to follow**
- **Step 1:** Create a fresh Google Doc named `SQL vs NoSQL Survey - <Your Name> - <Date>`.
- **Step 2:** Set share mode to `Anyone with link: Viewer` (don't leave it `Restricted` or reviewer cannot open it).
- **Step 3:** Pre-fill 6 Heading 1 sections in order:
  ```
  1. SQL taxonomy
  2. NoSQL taxonomy
  3. Decision table - data shape -> DB
  4. NestJS npm integration cheat-sheet
  5. 3 NestJS module config snippets
  6. References
  ```
- **Step 4:** At the very top, write a short paragraph (<= 100 words) answering "Why does a NestJS developer need to know both SQL and NoSQL?" in your own words, no copy/paste.

**Minimum acceptance criteria**
- The Google Doc has all **6 Heading 1 sections** in the listed order.
- Sharing = `Anyone with link: Viewer`; the link opens successfully in an incognito window.
- Opening paragraph is <= 100 words and is not a copy/paste from Wikipedia / ChatGPT (reviewer will paste the first sentence into Google; it must not match > 80%).

**Nice to have**
- Use the Google Docs auto Table of Contents.
- Add your name + email + LinkedIn link at the header so the reviewer can reach out.

translations.value: Tạo Google Docs trống và lập outline đúng 6 mục

**Các bước thực hiện**
- **Bước 1:** Tạo 1 Google Docs mới, đặt tên `SQL vs NoSQL Survey - <Họ tên> - <Ngày>`.
- **Bước 2:** Set share mode `Anyone with link: Viewer` (đừng để `Restricted`, reviewer sẽ không vào được).
- **Bước 3:** Dàn sẵn 6 Heading 1 đúng theo yêu cầu:
  ```
  1. Phân loại SQL
  2. Phân loại NoSQL
  3. Bảng quyết định "shape dữ liệu -> DB"
  4. Bảng tra cứu npm package tích hợp NestJS
  5. 3 snippet cấu hình NestJS module
  6. References
  ```
- **Bước 4:** Ở đầu docs, ghi 1 paragraph ngắn (≤ 100 từ) trả lời câu "Tại sao 1 dev NestJS cần biết cả SQL lẫn NoSQL?" - ghi bằng hiểu biết cá nhân, không copy.

**Yêu cầu tối thiểu cần đạt**
- Google Docs có đủ **6 Heading 1** đúng thứ tự như trên.
- Share mode = `Anyone with link: Viewer`; mở link ở chế độ ẩn danh (incognito) vẫn xem được.
- Paragraph mở đầu ≤ 100 từ, không phải copy paste từ Wikipedia / ChatGPT (reviewer sẽ paste 1 câu đầu vào Google, không được match quá 80%).

**Steps to follow**

**Minimum acceptance criteria**
- Section 1 lists **>= 5 SQL systems**, each with **>= 4 bullets** and at least one bullet referencing a concrete version/number.
- Section 2 covers **all 5 NoSQL families**, each with **>= 2 products** and **1 anti-use-case**.
- Each product explicitly documents (data model, consistency, license) - missing any of the three = not acceptable.
- No vague "fast, scales well" bullets without a technical reason.

steps.title: Write Section 3 - the "data shape -> DB" decision table with >= 6 real rows
steps.body:
**Steps to follow**
- **Step 1:** Insert a Google Docs table with 4 columns: `Data/query characteristic` | `Real use case` | `Recommended DB` | `Reason`.
- **Step 2:** Fill **>= 6 rows**, suggested examples (free to swap, just keep diversity):
  - Tight relational data + ACID transactions -> e.g. bank transfer, order + inventory -> `PostgreSQL` -> reason.
  - Constantly shifting schema, many optional fields -> e.g. product catalog, social user profile -> `MongoDB` -> reason.
  - Realtime counter / leaderboard / rate limit -> e.g. like count, session store -> `Redis` -> reason.
  - Full-text search, fuzzy match, relevance score -> e.g. Shopee product search, log analytics -> `Elasticsearch` / `OpenSearch` -> reason.
  - Dense time-series (IoT, metrics) -> `InfluxDB` / `TimescaleDB` -> reason.
  - Deep relational friend-of-friend / recommendations -> `Neo4j` -> reason.
  - Write-heavy horizontal scale, eventual consistency OK -> `Cassandra` / `ScyllaDB` -> reason.
- **Step 3:** The `Reason` column must cite **>= 1 technical keyword** per row (e.g. "row-level locking", "secondary index", "ZSET O(log N)", "inverted index", "LSM tree", "adjacency list traversal") rather than just "faster".

**Minimum acceptance criteria**
- An actual Google Docs table (via `Insert -> Table`, not ASCII art), 4 columns, **>= 6 rows**.
- Each row's `Real use case` is a **specific product scenario**, not "generic data management".
- Every `Reason` cell contains **>= 1 technical keyword** (from Step 3).
- No two rows pick the same DB with the same reason (shows genuine reasoning, not padding).

**Nice to have**
- Add a 5th column "What goes wrong if you pick wrong?" (e.g. Mongo for bank transfers -> multi-document transactions are hard).
- Add 1-2 rows about ***polyglot persistence*** combinations and why.

translations.value: Viết Mục 3 - Bảng quyết định "shape dữ liệu -> DB" với ≥ 6 dòng thực tế

**Các bước thực hiện**
- **Bước 1:** Tạo Google Docs Table 4 cột: `Đặc điểm dữ liệu / truy vấn` | `Use case thật` | `DB đề xuất` | `Lý do`.
- **Bước 2:** Điền **≥ 6 dòng**, ví dụ gợi ý (học viên được tự đổi miễn giữ tính đa dạng):
  - Dữ liệu quan hệ chặt + ACID transaction -> ví dụ: bank transfer, order + inventory -> `PostgreSQL` -> lý do.
  - Schema thay đổi liên tục, nhiều field optional -> ví dụ: product catalog, user profile social -> `MongoDB` -> lý do.
  - Counter realtime / leaderboard / rate limit -> ví dụ: like count, session store -> `Redis` -> lý do.
  - Full-text search, fuzzy match, relevance score -> ví dụ: search sản phẩm Shopee, log analytics -> `Elasticsearch` / `OpenSearch` -> lý do.
  - Chuỗi thời gian mật độ cao (IoT, metric) -> `InfluxDB` / `TimescaleDB` -> lý do.
  - Quan hệ đa cấp friend-of-friend, recommendation graph -> `Neo4j` -> lý do.
  - Write-heavy scale ngang, eventual consistency OK -> `Cassandra` / `ScyllaDB` -> lý do.
- **Bước 3:** Cột `Lý do` phải đi kèm **1 từ khoá kỹ thuật** (ví dụ: "row-level locking", "secondary index", "ZSET O(log N)", "inverted index", "LSM tree", "adjacency list traversal") chứ không chỉ nói "nhanh hơn".

**Yêu cầu tối thiểu cần đạt**
- Bảng Google Docs (thật, dùng tính năng `Insert -> Table`, không phải ASCII) với đủ 4 cột, **≥ 6 dòng**.
- Mỗi dòng có cột `Use case thật` là **1 tình huống sản phẩm cụ thể**, không viết chung "quản lý dữ liệu".
- Cột `Lý do` mỗi dòng chứa **≥ 1 từ khoá kỹ thuật** (liệt kê ở Bước 3).
- Không có 2 dòng chọn cùng 1 DB với lý do giống nhau (thể hiện đã suy nghĩ khác biệt).

**Nice to have**
- Thêm cột thứ 5 "Nếu chọn sai sẽ gặp vấn đề gì?" (ví dụ: dùng Mongo cho bank transfer -> khó transaction đa document).
- Thêm 1-2 dòng về ***polyglot persistence*** (dùng kết hợp) và lý do.

steps.title: Write Section 4 - the NestJS npm cheat-sheet and verify every package via `npm view`
steps.body:
**Steps to follow**
- **Step 1:** Insert a 4-column Google Docs table: `DB / kind` | `ORM / Driver` | `npm package` | `Docs link`.

  ```bash
  npm view @nestjs/typeorm version
  npm view @nestjs/mongoose version

  ```

**Minimum acceptance criteria**
- Table has **>= 10 rows**; every `npm package` returns a real version from `npm view <name> version` (no `npm ERR! 404`).
- **>= 1 screenshot** of `npm view ... version` output is pasted inside Section 4.
- All `Docs link` URLs open successfully and belong to official domains (`docs.nestjs.com`, `typeorm.io`, `mongoosejs.com`, `redis.io`, `elastic.co`, etc.) - NOT `medium.com`, `dev.to`, `stackoverflow.com`.

contents.title: Master PostgreSQL with TypeORM
contents.description: Learn how to define Entities, set up One-to-One, One-to-Many, and Many-to-Many relationships, and integrate TypeORM with PostgreSQL in NestJS.
contents.body:
## I. Introduction

Many developers working with relational databases write long raw **SQL** statements directly for table creation, querying, and updates. This is time-consuming and error-prone, especially as systems grow with many linked tables.

**TypeORM** addresses this by letting you define **Entities** in TypeScript, then translating them into corresponding **SQL** operations behind the scenes. This lesson helps you use TypeORM to manage schema, model relationships, and operate data in a structured way.

## II. Essence

This lesson follows a **source-first** approach: read the real flow `Entity -> Service -> Repository`, then test APIs to see exactly how TypeORM maps TypeScript classes to PostgreSQL tables and handles relationships.

Clone [here](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/tree/main/fullstack-mastery/typeorm-and-postgresql)

### Runtime Dependency Diagram

```mermaid
graph LR
    Client((Client))
    Client --> CatsController[CatsController]
    CatsController --> CatsService[CatsService]
    CatsService --> CatRepo[Repository<CatEntity>]
    CatRepo --> CatEntity[CatEntity + relations]
    CatRepo --> PG[(PostgreSQL)]
```

### Source Code Tree (File Level)

```mermaid
treeView-beta
    "src"
        "app.module.ts"
        "modules"
            "cats"
                "cats.module.ts"
                "cats.controller.ts"
                "cats.service.ts"
                "entities"
                    "cat.entity.ts"
                    "cat-passport.entity.ts"
                    "toy.entity.ts"
                    "owner.entity.ts"
                "dto/create-cat.dto.ts"
```

### Environment Setup and Run Flow

- **1. Prerequisites:** Require `Node.js LTS`, `npm`, Docker Desktop, and git.
- **2. Clone source demo:** Clone/pull source to work in the right context:
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources.git
  cd resources/fullstack-mastery/typeorm-and-postgresql
  git pull origin main
  ```
- **3. Start PostgreSQL:** Run the database container:
  ```bash
  docker compose -f .docker/postgresql.yaml up --build -d
  ```
- **4. Install dependencies and run app:** Install packages and start dev server:
  ```bash
  npm install
  npm run start:dev
  ```
- **5. Success signal:** App starts on port `3000`; TypeORM creates tables `cats`, `toys`, `owners`, `cat_passports`.

### Application Testing

- **Step 1:** Create a new cat with cascade relationships.

  **API Title:** **Cats API - create cat with relations - POST http://localhost:3000/cats**

  **How to call API:** Use Postman to send `POST` to `http://localhost:3000/cats`.

  **Body JSON:**
  ```json
  {
    "name": "Tom",
    "age": 3,
    "passport": { "issuedAt": "2024-01-01" },
    "toys": [{ "name": "Ball" }],
    "owners": [{ "name": "Alice" }]
  }
  ```

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/cats \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"name":"Tom","age":3,"passport":{"issuedAt":"2024-01-01"},"toys":[{"name":"Ball"}],"owners":[{"name":"Alice"}]}'
  ```

- **Step 2:** Read cat details to confirm relations were persisted.

  **API Title:** **Cats API - get one cat with relations - GET http://localhost:3000/cats/1**

  **How to call API:** Use Postman to send `GET` to `http://localhost:3000/cats/1`.

  **JSON Body:** No body for `GET`.

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl http://localhost:3000/cats/1
  ```

  **Trace code execution (by file):**
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts:24`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/typeorm-and-postgresql/src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts#L24) -> `CatsController.create()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:29`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/typeorm-and-postgresql/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L29) -> `CatsService.create()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/entities/cat.entity.ts:11`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/typeorm-and-postgresql/src/modules/cats/entities/cat.entity.ts#L11) -> `CatEntity` relation decorators
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:53`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/typeorm-and-postgresql/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L53) -> `CatsService.findOne()`

  *Expected result:* Returned data includes the cat and saved relations (`passport`, `toys`, `owners`) correctly.

  *Conclusion:* TypeORM reduces manual SQL through entity/relation mapping while preserving relational integrity on PostgreSQL.

## III. Core Concepts

### 1. ***Entity Mapping***

- **Role:** `@Entity`, `@Column` map TypeScript classes to PostgreSQL tables/columns.
- **Common mistake:** Declaring column types that do not match real data.
- **Production impact:** Type-cast query errors and risky migrations.

### 2. ***Relation Mapping***

- **Role:** `@OneToOne`, `@OneToMany`, `@ManyToMany` express domain relationships clearly.
- **Common mistake:** Setting overly broad cascade rules and unintentionally overwriting linked data.
- **Production impact:** Related data mutates in hard-to-control ways.

### 3. ***Indexing***

- **Role:** Speed up queries on frequently filtered/sorted columns.
- **Common mistake:** Missing indexes on hot query columns or over-indexing every column.
- **Production impact:** Slow reads or slow writes due to index maintenance overhead.

### 4. ***Transaction***

- **Role:** Ensure grouped DB operations all succeed or all rollback.
- **Common mistake:** Splitting multi-step writes without transaction boundaries.
- **Production impact:** Partial data states and business inconsistency.

## IV. Advanced Techniques

**TypeORM** becomes most powerful when used with deliberate architecture decisions: define aggregate boundaries for safe cascade usage, index based on real query patterns, and wrap critical write workflows in transactions.

In production, combining these techniques with migration discipline and query profiling helps you keep PostgreSQL both consistent and performant as data volume grows.

## V. Interview Questions

1. **Interview Question:**  
   “In TypeORM, when should you enable `cascade: true`, and when should you avoid it?”
   - **What is being assessed:** Understanding relation lifecycle and chain-write risks.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Use cascade for clear aggregate boundaries; avoid blind cascade on shared relations to prevent accidental writes.

2. **Interview Question:**  
   “Why can querying by `name` be slow even with only a few hundred thousand records?”
   - **What is being assessed:** Ability to read execution plans and reason about indexing.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Point out missing/ineffective index possibilities; propose adding the correct index and measuring again.

3. **Interview Question:**  
   “How do you implement a transfer A -> B with TypeORM so data is never lost on mid-flow failure?”
   - **What is being assessed:** Ability to apply transactions in critical business workflows.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Use transactions (`QueryRunner`/transaction manager) and rollback if any step fails.

translations.value: Làm chủ PostgreSQL với TypeORM
Học cách định nghĩa Entity, thiết lập các mối quan hệ One-to-One, One-to-Many, Many-to-Many, và thực hành tích hợp TypeORM với PostgreSQL trong NestJS.

## I. Lời mở đầu

Nhiều lập trình viên khi làm việc với cơ sở dữ liệu quan hệ thường viết trực tiếp các câu lệnh **SQL** dài dòng để tạo bảng, truy vấn và cập nhật dữ liệu. Cách làm này không chỉ mất thời gian mà còn dễ gặp lỗi khi hệ thống lớn dần với hàng chục bảng liên kết chồng chéo.

**TypeORM** xuất hiện để giải quyết vấn đề này — bạn chỉ cần định nghĩa các **Entity** bằng TypeScript, và TypeORM sẽ tự động dịch chúng thành các lệnh **SQL** tương ứng phía sau. Bài học này sẽ giúp bạn hiểu cách sử dụng TypeORM để quản lý schema, thiết lập quan hệ và thao tác dữ liệu một cách mạch lạc.

## II. Bản chất

Bài này đi theo hướng **source-first**: đọc flow thật từ `Entity -> Service -> Repository` trước, sau đó test API để thấy rõ cách TypeORM map class TypeScript sang bảng PostgreSQL và xử lý quan hệ.

Clone tại [đây](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/tree/main/fullstack-mastery/typeorm-and-postgresql)

### Sơ đồ phụ thuộc runtime

```mermaid
graph LR
    Client((Client))
    Client --> CatsController[CatsController]
    CatsController --> CatsService[CatsService]
    CatsService --> CatRepo[Repository<CatEntity>]
    CatRepo --> CatEntity[CatEntity + relations]
    CatRepo --> PG[(PostgreSQL)]
```

### Sơ đồ cây source code (file-level)

```mermaid
treeView-beta
    "src"
        "app.module.ts"
        "modules"
            "cats"
                "cats.module.ts"
                "cats.controller.ts"
                "cats.service.ts"
                "entities"
                    "cat.entity.ts"
                    "cat-passport.entity.ts"
                    "toy.entity.ts"
                    "owner.entity.ts"
                "dto/create-cat.dto.ts"
```

### Chuẩn bị Môi trường và Luồng Cài đặt

- **1. Prerequisites:** Cần `Node.js LTS`, `npm`, Docker Desktop và git.
- **2. Clone source demo:** Clone/pull source để đọc đúng context code:
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources.git
  cd resources/fullstack-mastery/typeorm-and-postgresql
  git pull origin main
  ```
- **3. Khởi động PostgreSQL:** Chạy container database:
  ```bash
  docker compose -f .docker/postgresql.yaml up --build -d
  ```
- **4. Cài dependency và chạy app:** Cài package rồi start dev server:
  ```bash
  npm install
  npm run start:dev
  ```
- **5. Tín hiệu thành công:** App start cổng `3000`; TypeORM tạo bảng `cats`, `toys`, `owners`, `cat_passports`.

### Kiểm thử ứng dụng

- **Bước 1:** Tạo cat mới kèm quan hệ cascade.

  **Tiêu đề API:** **Cats API - create cat with relations - POST http://localhost:3000/cats**

  **Hướng dẫn gọi API:** Dùng Postman gửi `POST` tới `http://localhost:3000/cats`.

  **Body JSON:**
  ```json
  {
    "name": "Tom",
    "age": 3,
    "passport": { "issuedAt": "2024-01-01" },
    "toys": [{ "name": "Ball" }],
    "owners": [{ "name": "Alice" }]
  }
  ```

  Hoặc dùng **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/cats \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"name":"Tom","age":3,"passport":{"issuedAt":"2024-01-01"},"toys":[{"name":"Ball"}],"owners":[{"name":"Alice"}]}'
  ```

- **Bước 2:** Đọc chi tiết cat để xác nhận quan hệ đã persist.

  **Tiêu đề API:** **Cats API - get one cat with relations - GET http://localhost:3000/cats/1**

  **Hướng dẫn gọi API:** Dùng Postman gửi `GET` tới `http://localhost:3000/cats/1`.

  **Body JSON:** Không có body với request `GET`.

  Hoặc dùng **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl http://localhost:3000/cats/1
  ```

  **Trace code execution (theo file):**
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts:24`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/typeorm-and-postgresql/src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts#L24) -> `CatsController.create()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:29`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/typeorm-and-postgresql/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L29) -> `CatsService.create()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/entities/cat.entity.ts:11`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/typeorm-and-postgresql/src/modules/cats/entities/cat.entity.ts#L11) -> `CatEntity` relation decorators
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:53`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/typeorm-and-postgresql/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L53) -> `CatsService.findOne()`

  *Kết quả mong đợi:* Dữ liệu trả về gồm cat và các quan hệ (`passport`, `toys`, `owners`) đã lưu đúng.

  *Kết luận:* TypeORM giảm SQL thủ công bằng mapping entity/relation, đồng thời vẫn giữ được tính toàn vẹn quan hệ trên PostgreSQL.

## III. Các khái niệm cốt lõi

### 1. ***Entity Mapping***

- **Vai trò:** `@Entity`, `@Column` ánh xạ class TypeScript thành bảng/cột PostgreSQL.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Khai báo kiểu cột không khớp dữ liệu thực tế.
- **Hậu quả production:** Query lỗi cast type, migration phát sinh rủi ro.

### 2. ***Relation Mapping***

- **Vai trò:** `@OneToOne`, `@OneToMany`, `@ManyToMany` mô tả quan hệ domain rõ ràng.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Đặt cascade quá rộng, ghi đè dữ liệu liên kết ngoài ý muốn.
- **Hậu quả production:** Dữ liệu liên đới bị mutate khó kiểm soát.

### 3. ***Indexing***

- **Vai trò:** Tăng tốc truy vấn cho các cột filter/sort thường dùng.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Quên index cột truy vấn nóng hoặc lạm dụng index trên mọi cột.
- **Hậu quả production:** Chậm đọc hoặc chậm ghi do index maintenance quá nặng.

### 4. ***Transaction***

- **Vai trò:** Đảm bảo nhóm thao tác DB thành công toàn bộ hoặc rollback toàn bộ.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Chia nhiều thao tác ghi mà không bọc transaction.
- **Hậu quả production:** Trạng thái dữ liệu dở dang, sai lệch nghiệp vụ.

## IV. Kết luận

**TypeORM** là cầu nối mạnh mẽ giữa **TypeScript** và **PostgreSQL**, giúp bạn định nghĩa schema bằng code, thiết lập quan hệ bằng decorator và tối ưu truy vấn bằng indexing. Cascade save đơn giản hóa việc thao tác dữ liệu phức tạp, trong khi Transaction đảm bảo tính toàn vẹn tuyệt đối.

**Kết luận:** Làm chủ TypeORM không chỉ là biết viết Entity — mà là hiểu cách thiết kế quan hệ, tối ưu hiệu năng và đảm bảo dữ liệu luôn nhất quán trong mọi tình huống.

## V. Các mẫu câu phỏng vấn

1. **Câu hỏi phỏng vấn:**  
   “Trong TypeORM, khi nào nên bật `cascade: true` và khi nào nên tránh?”
   - **Ý cần đánh giá:** Mức độ hiểu về lifecycle relation và rủi ro ghi dữ liệu dây chuyền.
   - **Hướng trả lời kỳ vọng:** Dùng cascade cho aggregate boundary rõ ràng; tránh cascade mù ở quan hệ shared để không ghi nhầm dữ liệu.

2. **Câu hỏi phỏng vấn:**  
   “Vì sao query theo `name` chậm dù dữ liệu chỉ vài trăm nghìn bản ghi?”
   - **Ý cần đánh giá:** Năng lực đọc execution plan và tư duy index.
   - **Hướng trả lời kỳ vọng:** Chỉ ra khả năng thiếu index hoặc dùng index không hiệu quả; đề xuất thêm index đúng cột và đo lại.

3. **Câu hỏi phỏng vấn:**  
   “Bạn xử lý chuyển tiền A -> B bằng TypeORM như thế nào để không mất dữ liệu khi lỗi giữa chừng?”
   - **Ý cần đánh giá:** Khả năng áp dụng transaction trong nghiệp vụ quan trọng.
   - **Hướng trả lời kỳ vọng:** Dùng transaction (`QueryRunner`/manager transaction), rollback nếu bất kỳ bước nào thất bại.


### Environment Setup and Run Flow

- **1. Prerequisites:** Require `Node.js LTS`, `npm`, Docker Desktop, and git.
- **2. Clone source demo:** Clone/pull source to work in the right context:
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources.git
  cd resources/fullstack-mastery/typeorm-and-postgresql
  git pull origin main
  ```
- **3. Start PostgreSQL:** Run the database container:
  ```bash
  docker compose -f .docker/postgresql.yaml up --build -d
  ```
- **4. Install dependencies and run app:** Install packages and start dev server:
  ```bash
  npm install
  npm run start:dev
  ```
- **5. Success signal:** App starts on port `3000`; TypeORM creates tables `cats`, `toys`, `owners`, `cat_passports`.

### Application Testing

- **Step 1:** Create a new cat with cascade relationships.

  **API Title:** **Cats API - create cat with relations - POST http://localhost:3000/cats**

  **How to call API:** Use Postman to send `POST` to `http://localhost:3000/cats`.

  **Body JSON:**
  ```json
  {
    "name": "Tom",
    "age": 3,
    "passport": { "issuedAt": "2024-01-01" },
    "toys": [{ "name": "Ball" }],
    "owners": [{ "name": "Alice" }]
  }
  ```

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/cats \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"name":"Tom","age":3,"passport":{"issuedAt":"2024-01-01"},"toys":[{"name":"Ball"}],"owners":[{"name":"Alice"}]}'
  ```

- **Step 2:** Read cat details to confirm relations were persisted.

  **API Title:** **Cats API - get one cat with relations - GET http://localhost:3000/cats/1**

  **How to call API:** Use Postman to send `GET` to `http://localhost:3000/cats/1`.

  **JSON Body:** No body for `GET`.

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl http://localhost:3000/cats/1
  ```

  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts:24`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/typeorm-and-postgresql/src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts#L24) -> `CatsController.create()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:29`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/typeorm-and-postgresql/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L29) -> `CatsService.create()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/entities/cat.entity.ts:11`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/typeorm-and-postgresql/src/modules/cats/entities/cat.entity.ts#L11) -> `CatEntity` relation decorators
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:53`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/typeorm-and-postgresql/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L53) -> `CatsService.findOne()`

  *Expected result:* Returned data includes the cat and saved relations (`passport`, `toys`, `owners`) correctly.

  *Conclusion:* TypeORM reduces manual SQL through entity/relation mapping while preserving relational integrity on PostgreSQL.

## III. Core Concepts

### 1. ***Entity Mapping***

- **Role:** `@Entity`, `@Column` map TypeScript classes to PostgreSQL tables/columns.
- **Common mistake:** Declaring column types that do not match real data.
- **Production impact:** Type-cast query errors and risky migrations.

### 2. ***Relation Mapping***

- **Role:** `@OneToOne`, `@OneToMany`, `@ManyToMany` express domain relationships clearly.
- **Common mistake:** Setting overly broad cascade rules and unintentionally overwriting linked data.
- **Production impact:** Related data mutates in hard-to-control ways.

### 3. ***Indexing***

- **Role:** Speed up queries on frequently filtered/sorted columns.
- **Common mistake:** Missing indexes on hot query columns or over-indexing every column.
- **Production impact:** Slow reads or slow writes due to index maintenance overhead.

### 4. ***Transaction***

- **Role:** Ensure grouped DB operations all succeed or all rollback.
- **Common mistake:** Splitting multi-step writes without transaction boundaries.
- **Production impact:** Partial data states and business inconsistency.

## IV. Advanced Techniques

**TypeORM** becomes most powerful when used with deliberate architecture decisions: define aggregate boundaries for safe cascade usage, index based on real query patterns, and wrap critical write workflows in transactions.

In production, combining these techniques with migration discipline and query profiling helps you keep PostgreSQL both consistent and performant as data volume grows.

## V. Interview Questions

1. **Interview Question:**  
   “In TypeORM, when should you enable `cascade: true`, and when should you avoid it?”
   - **What is being assessed:** Understanding relation lifecycle and chain-write risks.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Use cascade for clear aggregate boundaries; avoid blind cascade on shared relations to prevent accidental writes.

2. **Interview Question:**  
   “Why can querying by `name` be slow even with only a few hundred thousand records?”
   - **What is being assessed:** Ability to read execution plans and reason about indexing.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Point out missing/ineffective index possibilities; propose adding the correct index and measuring again.

3. **Interview Question:**  
   “How do you implement a transfer A -> B with TypeORM so data is never lost on mid-flow failure?”
   - **What is being assessed:** Ability to apply transactions in critical business workflows.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Use transactions (`QueryRunner`/transaction manager) and rollback if any step fails.

challenges.title: Library CRUD with TypeORM + PostgreSQL (Author 1-n Book n-n Tag) and real migrations
challenges.description: Build a NestJS Library app using TypeORM on a real PostgreSQL running via docker-compose. The domain has 3 entities with 2 relation types: Author 1-n Book, Book n-n Tag. You MUST manage schema via migration CLI (never synchronize: true) and produce 2 migrations: one to init all 3 tables plus the booktags join table, and a separate one to add a column Book.publishedYear after the schema already exists (mimicking a real deploy -> new field -> new migration workflow). CRUD uses Repository; the filter GET /books?tag=... uses QueryBuilder with innerJoin on booktags.
challenges.requirements:
Create a ***NestJS*** project `library-typeorm-postgres`:
- **docker-compose.yml** at the root starts Postgres 16 (port `5432`, user/password/db read from `.env`); the project must come up via `docker compose up -d` and `npm run start:dev` must connect.
- **3 entities** under `src/<feature>/entities/`:
  - `Author` (`id` UUID PK, `name` varchar NOT NULL, `bio` text nullable, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`). Relation `@OneToMany(() => Book, (b) => b.author)`.
  - `Book` (`id` UUID PK, `title` varchar NOT NULL, `publishedYear` int - **added in migration 2**, `authorId` FK, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`). Relation `@ManyToOne(() => Author, { onDelete: 'CASCADE' })` on `author`; `@ManyToMany(() => Tag)` with `@JoinTable({ name: 'book_tags' })`.
  - `Tag` (`id` UUID PK, `name` varchar UNIQUE NOT NULL). Relation `@ManyToMany(() => Book, (b) => b.tags)`.
- **2 migrations** under `src/migrations/`:
  - `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS-init-schema.ts`: create 3 tables `authors`, `books`, `tags` + join `book_tags` + FK + index on `books.author_id`.
  - `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS-add-book-published-year.ts`: `ALTER TABLE books ADD COLUMN published_year int NULL`. Provide both `up()` and `down()` (down drops the column).
- **`ormconfig` / `DataSource`** lives in `src/database/data-source.ts` and default-exports one `DataSource` for the migration CLI. `TypeOrmModule.forRootAsync` in `AppModule` reads config via `ConfigService`; `synchronize: false` and `migrationsRun: false` are MANDATORY across all envs.
- **CRUD endpoints**:
  - `POST /authors` { name, bio? } -> 201.
  - `POST /books` { title, authorId, tagIds: string[] } -> 201 (validate authorId + tagIds exist, otherwise 404).
  - `POST /tags` { name } -> 201 (unique).
  - `GET /authors/:id/books` -> returns the `Author` with an eager-loaded `books[]` array (`relations: ['books']`).
  - `GET /books?tag=<tagName>` -> `QueryBuilder` using `innerJoin book_tags` + `innerJoin tags` filtered by `tags.name`, returns `Book[]` plus their `tags`.
- **`package.json` scripts**:
  ```
  "typeorm": "typeorm-ts-node-commonjs",
  "migration:generate": "npm run typeorm -- migration:generate -d src/database/data-source.ts",
  "migration:run":      "npm run typeorm -- migration:run -d src/database/data-source.ts",
  "migration:revert":   "npm run typeorm -- migration:revert -d src/database/data-source.ts"
  ```
- **README** must include an ERD (ASCII or Mermaid image) and a **Smoke Test** section with the real output of 3 requests plus a `psql \dt` snapshot showing 4 tables.

**Forbidden:**
- `synchronize: true` anywhere -> **0 for the migration prompt**.
- Lazy relation (`Promise<Book[]>`) without `await` -> response returns a Promise string -> **0 for the whole challenge**.
- Committing a real `.env`; commit only `.env.example`.

steps.title: Bootstrap the project and the Postgres docker-compose
steps.body:
**Steps to follow**
- **Step 1:** Create the project and install deps:
  ```bash
  nest new library-typeorm-postgres
  cd library-typeorm-postgres
  npm i @nestjs/typeorm typeorm pg @nestjs/config class-validator class-transformer
  npm i -D @types/pg
  ```
- **Step 2:** Create `docker-compose.yml`:
  ```yaml
  services:
    postgres:
      image: postgres:16
      ports: ["5432:5432"]
      environment:
        POSTGRES_DB: library
        POSTGRES_USER: library
        POSTGRES_PASSWORD: library
      volumes: ["pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data"]
  volumes:
    pgdata:
  ```
  Run:
  ```bash
  docker compose up -d
  ```
- **Step 3:** Create `.env` + `.env.example` with `DB_HOST=localhost`, `DB_PORT=5432`, `DB_USER=library`, `DB_PASSWORD=library`, `DB_NAME=library`. Add `.env` to `.gitignore`.
- **Step 4:** Scaffold the skeleton:
  ```bash
  nest g module database
  nest g module author
  nest g module book
  nest g module tag
  ```

**Minimum acceptance criteria**
- `docker compose up -d` starts Postgres successfully; `docker ps` shows the `postgres:16` container.
- `psql -h localhost -U library -d library` logs in with the `.env` password.
- `.env.example` is committed; the real `.env` sits in `.gitignore`.
- `npm run start:dev` boots without missing-module errors.

**Nice to have**
- Add a `pgadmin` or `adminer` service in `docker-compose.yml` to browse the DB via UI.
- Add `npm run db:up` aliasing `docker compose up -d`.

steps.title: Write and run migration 1 (init schema) via the CLI
steps.body:
**Steps to follow**
- **Step 1:** Add scripts to `package.json`:
  ```json
  "scripts": {
    "typeorm": "typeorm-ts-node-commonjs",
    "migration:generate": "npm run typeorm -- migration:generate -d src/database/data-source.ts",
    "migration:run":      "npm run typeorm -- migration:run -d src/database/data-source.ts",
    "migration:revert":   "npm run typeorm -- migration:revert -d src/database/data-source.ts"
  }
  ```
- **Step 2:** Generate the init migration from the entities:
  ```bash
  npm run migration:generate -- src/migrations/InitSchema
  ```
  Open `src/migrations/<timestamp>-InitSchema.ts` and verify there are 4 `CREATE TABLE` statements (`authors`, `books`, `tags`, `book_tags`) + FKs + the `tags.name` unique index.
- **Step 3:** Run the migration:
  ```bash
  npm run migration:run
  ```
- **Step 4:** Verify through psql:
  ```bash
  docker exec -it <container> psql -U library -d library -c "\dt"
  ```
  You should see 4 business tables + the `migrations` tracking table.
- **Step 5:** Test revert:
  ```bash
  npm run migration:revert
  ```
  Confirm `\dt` shows only the `migrations` table, then run `migration:run` again to restore.

**Minimum acceptance criteria**
- `npm run migration:run` succeeds on an empty DB with the log `Migration "InitSchema<timestamp>" has been executed successfully`.
- `psql \dt` shows **exactly 5 tables**: `authors`, `books`, `tags`, `book_tags`, `migrations`.
- FK `books.author_id -> authors.id` exists (verify via `\d books`).
- `npm run migration:revert` drops all 4 business tables; a subsequent `migration:run` restores them.

**Nice to have**
- Declare `idx_books_author_id` explicitly in migration 1 instead of relying on TypeORM's default.
- Write a `db:seed` script inserting 2 authors + 5 books + 3 tags for smoke tests.

steps.title: Implement the CRUD + QueryBuilder tag filter
steps.body:
**Steps to follow**
- **Step 1:** In each module (`author`, `book`, `tag`) import `TypeOrmModule.forFeature([<Entity>])` and inject `@InjectRepository(<Entity>)` into the service.
- **Step 2:** `AuthorService`: `create(dto)`, `findById(id, { relations: ['books'] })`.
- **Step 3:** `TagService`: `create(dto)` throws `ConflictException` on duplicate name.
- **Step 4:** `BookService.create(dto)`:
  ```ts
  async create(dto: CreateBookDto) {
    const author = await this.authorRepo.findOneBy({ id: dto.authorId });
    if (!author) throw new NotFoundException('author not found');
    const tags = await this.tagRepo.findBy({ id: In(dto.tagIds) });
    if (tags.length !== dto.tagIds.length) throw new NotFoundException('tag not found');
    const book = this.bookRepo.create({ title: dto.title, author, tags });
    return this.bookRepo.save(book);
  }
  ```
- **Step 5:** `BookService.findByTag(tagName)` uses `QueryBuilder`:
  ```ts
  return this.bookRepo.createQueryBuilder('book')
    .innerJoinAndSelect('book.tags', 'tag')
    .where('tag.name = :n', { n: tagName })
    .getMany();
  ```
- **Step 6:** Matching controllers, DTOs + a global `new ValidationPipe({ whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true, transform: true })` in `main.ts`.
- **Step 7:** `AuthorController.getBooks(@Param('id') id)` calls `authorRepo.findOne({ where: { id }, relations: ['books'] })`; if null -> `NotFoundException`.

**Minimum acceptance criteria**
- `POST /authors`, `POST /tags`, `POST /books` all return 201 with valid JSON; validation failures return 400 with `class-validator` messages.
- `POST /books` with a non-existent `authorId` -> 404 `author not found`; an unknown `tagId` -> 404 `tag not found`.
- `GET /authors/:id/books` returns JSON with `id`, `name`, and `books: [...]` (may be empty when no book exists).
- `GET /books?tag=<name>` returns only books tagged accordingly; an unknown tag returns `[]` (NOT 404).
- No `Promise` string appears in responses (no lazy-relation leak).

**Nice to have**
- Add pagination (`?page`, `?size`) to `GET /books`.
- Add a default `GET /books` returning the 20 most-recent items ordered by `createdAt desc`.
- Use separate DTOs + response interfaces so internal columns don't leak.

steps.title: Migration 2 - add Book.publishedYear and apply against a DB that already has data
steps.body:
**Steps to follow**
- **Step 1:** Seed at least 2 authors + 3 books + 2 tags through Postman to mimic a "prod" DB that already has data.
- **Step 2:** Open `book.entity.ts` and add:
  ```ts
  @Column({ name: 'published_year', type: 'int', nullable: true })
  publishedYear: number | null;
  ```
- **Step 3:** Generate the diff migration:
  ```bash
  npm run migration:generate -- src/migrations/AddBookPublishedYear
  ```
- **Step 4:** Open the new migration, verify `up()` has `ADD COLUMN "published_year"` (nullable) and `down()` has `DROP COLUMN "published_year"`. If TypeORM generates a NOT NULL column without a default (which would fail on a table with data) -> manually switch to `nullable: true`.
- **Step 5:** Run:
  ```bash
  npm run migration:run
  ```
  Confirm success and that the old rows remain (`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM books` unchanged).
- **Step 6:** Test revert:
  ```bash
  npm run migration:revert
  ```
  Verify the column is gone (`\d books` no longer shows `published_year`); rerun `migration:run`.
- **Step 7:** Update `CreateBookDto` + `UpdateBookDto` to optionally accept `publishedYear`; confirm `POST /books` with `{title, authorId, tagIds, publishedYear: 2024}` persists the value.

**Minimum acceptance criteria**
- `src/migrations/` contains **exactly 2 migration files** (InitSchema + AddBookPublishedYear) with ascending timestamps.
- After migration 2, `\d books` shows `published_year int NULL`; `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM books` keeps the previous row count (no data loss).
- `npm run migration:revert` drops just `published_year`, leaving other columns intact.
- `POST /books` with `publishedYear: 2024` persists `publishedYear=2024`; omitting the field stores `NULL`.

**Nice to have**
- Make the migration idempotent via a `hasColumn` check before add/drop.
- Add a `CHECK` constraint `published_year BETWEEN 1000 AND 2100`.

steps.title: Smoke-test 3 scenarios via Postman/curl and paste the output into the README
steps.body:
**Steps to follow**
- **Step 1:** Run `docker compose up -d` + `npm run migration:run` + `npm run start:dev`.
- **Step 2:** Create an author:

  **API name:** **Author API - create author - POST http://localhost:3000/authors**

  **How to call:** Use Postman to send `POST` to `http://localhost:3000/authors`, in the `Body` tab pick `raw` -> `JSON`.

  **JSON Body:** `{"name":"George Orwell","bio":"English novelist"}`

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/authors \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"name":"George Orwell","bio":"English novelist"}'
  ```
- **Step 3:** Create 2 tags (`POST /tags` with `{"name":"dystopia"}` and `{"name":"classic"}`) and capture their ids.
- **Step 4:** Create a book with both tags and a `publishedYear`:

  **API name:** **Book API - create book with tags - POST http://localhost:3000/books**

  **How to call:** Use Postman to send `POST` to `http://localhost:3000/books`, in the `Body` tab pick `raw` -> `JSON`.

  **JSON Body:** `{"title":"1984","authorId":"<authorId>","tagIds":["<tagId1>","<tagId2>"],"publishedYear":1949}`

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/books \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"title":"1984","authorId":"<authorId>","tagIds":["<tagId1>","<tagId2>"],"publishedYear":1949}'
  ```
- **Step 5:** Verify eager load:

  **API name:** **Author API - get author with books - GET http://localhost:3000/authors/<authorId>/books**

  **How to call:** Use Postman to send `GET` to `http://localhost:3000/authors/<authorId>/books`.

  **JSON Body:** No body for `GET` requests.

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl http://localhost:3000/authors/<authorId>/books
  ```
- **Step 6:** Verify the QueryBuilder filter:

  **API name:** **Book API - filter by tag - GET http://localhost:3000/books?tag=dystopia**

  **How to call:** Use Postman to send `GET` to `http://localhost:3000/books?tag=dystopia`.

  **JSON Body:** No body for `GET` requests.

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl "http://localhost:3000/books?tag=dystopia"
  ```
- **Step 7:** In `README.md` under **Smoke Test**, paste the 4 real JSON responses (create author, create book, get author with books, filter by tag) + one screenshot of `psql \dt` showing 5 tables + one screenshot of the successful migration run log.
- **Step 8:** Draw the ERD in the README using Mermaid:
  ```
  erDiagram
    AUTHORS ||--o{ BOOKS : writes
    BOOKS }o--o{ TAGS : tagged_with
  ```

**Minimum acceptance criteria**
- The 4 scenarios return HTTP 201/200; `GET /authors/:id/books` has a `books: [...]` array containing the book just created.
- `GET /books?tag=dystopia` returns an array containing `"1984"`; `GET /books?tag=does-not-exist` returns `[]` (not 404, not 500).
- The README contains a rendered Mermaid ERD and a **Smoke Test** section with the 4 real JSON responses + 2 screenshots (psql \dt + migration log).
- Deleting an `author` (`DELETE /authors/:id` if implemented) cascades and removes their books (verify with `SELECT COUNT` before/after) thanks to `onDelete: 'CASCADE'`.

**Nice to have**
- Add `DELETE /authors/:id` to test cascade.
- Export a Postman Collection to `docs/postman/library.postman_collection.json`.
- Include a GIF of migrate -> create -> query in the README.

challenges.title: Advanced TypeORM - index strategy, jsonb column, 1-1/1-n/n-n relations with cascade and auto timestamp
challenges.description: Upgrade the EASY project library-typeorm-postgres to a hands-on TypeORM level focused on library features every production dev must master: (1) indexes - single-column, composite, unique partial, GIN for full-text search; (2) jsonb column on Postgres (not Mongo's BSON - TypeORM maps it to the jsonb type for structured binary JSON) to store Book.metadata with a loose schema, queryable via operators -> and @>; (3) full relation coverage: Author 1-1 AuthorProfile (shared PK), Author 1-n Book, Book 1-n Review, Book n-n Tag; (4) cascade in the right places - save cascade for profile/reviews/tags, onDelete CASCADE for profile/reviews but RESTRICT for tag (tags must outlive books); (5) auto timestamps @CreateDateColumn + @UpdateDateColumn + @DeleteDateColumn with DB-side defaults and a @BeforeUpdate hook to prove it works.
challenges.requirements:
Fork the EASY project to `library-typeorm-advanced-features`. Extend as follows:

**New / changed entities:**
- **`AuthorProfile`** (1-1 with `Author` via **shared PK**):
  - `id` UUID PK that is also FK to `authors.id` (use `@OneToOne` + `@JoinColumn` + `@PrimaryColumn`).
  - `avatarUrl` varchar.
  - `social` jsonb `{ twitter?: string, github?: string, website?: string }`.
  - `stats` jsonb `{ totalBooks: number, totalReviews: number, avgRating: number }` (read-mostly, recomputed by service).
  - `@CreateDateColumn`, `@UpdateDateColumn`.
- **`Review`** (1-n from `Book`):
  - `id` UUID PK.
  - `bookId` FK, relation `@ManyToOne(() => Book, { onDelete: 'CASCADE' })`.
  - `reviewerName` varchar NOT NULL.
  - `rating` smallint CHECK `BETWEEN 1 AND 5`.
  - `comment` text nullable.
  - `@CreateDateColumn` only (no updatedAt).
- **`Book` updated**:
  - Add `@Column({ type: 'jsonb', default: {} }) metadata: { isbn?: string; pages?: number; language?: string; coverUrl?: string; }`.
  - Add `@Column({ type: 'tsvector', nullable: true, select: false }) searchVector: any;` populated via a DB-side trigger when `title` changes (setup in migration, NOT in app).
  - Relation `@OneToMany(() => Review, (r) => r.book, { cascade: ['insert'] }) reviews: Review[];`.
  - Keep `@ManyToMany(() => Tag, { cascade: ['insert'] })` - DO NOT put `onDelete: 'CASCADE'` from the pivot `book_tags` to the Tag side (tags must remain).
- **`Author` updated**:
  - Add `@OneToOne(() => AuthorProfile, (p) => p.author, { cascade: true, eager: false }) profile?: AuthorProfile;`.
  - Keep EASY's `@OneToMany Book { onDelete: 'CASCADE' }`.

**Mandatory indexes (declare via `@Index` decorator, NO ad-hoc raw SQL floating around):**
- `@Index(['title'])` on `Book` - B-tree lookup by title.
- `@Index(['authorId', 'publishedYear'])` composite on `Book` - filter "books by author X in year Y".
- `@Index('uniq_book_isbn', ...)` **unique partial index**: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uniq_book_isbn ON books ((metadata->>'isbn')) WHERE metadata->>'isbn' IS NOT NULL;` (raw in migration because TypeORM decorator does not cover partial).
- `@Index('idx_book_search_vector', { synchronize: false })` GIN: `CREATE INDEX idx_book_search_vector ON books USING GIN (search_vector);` (raw in migration).
- `@Index(['rating'])` on `Review` - sort/filter by rating.
- `@Index(['bookId', 'rating'])` composite on `Review` - "top review per book".

**Migrations:**
- `CreateAuthorProfile` - creates `author_profiles` with shared PK + FK CASCADE.
- `CreateReview` - creates `reviews` + FK CASCADE + CHECK rating + 2 indexes (rating, composite).
- `AddBookMetadataJsonb` - adds `metadata jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb` + unique partial index `uniq_book_isbn`.
- `AddBookSearchVector` - adds `search_vector tsvector` + DB-side trigger:
  ```sql
  CREATE FUNCTION books_search_trigger() RETURNS trigger AS $$
  BEGIN NEW.search_vector := to_tsvector('english', coalesce(NEW.title, '')); RETURN NEW; END;
  $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
  CREATE TRIGGER books_search_update BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF title ON books
    FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION books_search_trigger();
  CREATE INDEX idx_book_search_vector ON books USING GIN(search_vector);
  ```
- Every migration must implement full `up()` and `down()`.

**New endpoints:**
- `POST /authors/:id/profile` body `{ avatarUrl, social, stats? }` -> cascade create via `authorRepo.save(author)` (NOT `profileRepo.save` directly - to demo cascade).
- `GET /authors/:id?withProfile=true` -> eager load profile when the query param is present; default does not load (entity is `eager: false`).
- `POST /books/:id/reviews` body `{ reviewerName, rating, comment? }` -> 201. Validate `rating 1-5` via `class-validator`. After insert, recompute `author.profile.stats` (totalReviews, avgRating) in the same transaction.
- `GET /books/search?q=<keyword>` -> full-text search via GIN index:
  ```ts
  this.bookRepo.createQueryBuilder('book')
    .where(`book.search_vector @@ to_tsquery('english', :q)`, { q: keyword.split(' ').join(' & ') })
    .orderBy(`ts_rank(book.search_vector, to_tsquery('english', :q))`, 'DESC')
  ```
- `GET /books/by-isbn/:isbn` -> `WHERE metadata->>'isbn' = :isbn` (verify unique partial index is used via `EXPLAIN`).
- `GET /books/by-language/:lang` -> `WHERE metadata->>'language' = :lang`.
- `POST /books` (already exists) accepts a full `metadata` object + nested `reviews[]` - cascade insert book + reviews in a single call.
- `DELETE /books/:id` -> cascade deletes `reviews`, does NOT delete tags; tags remain in the `tags` table (verify by count before/after).
- `DELETE /authors/:id` -> cascade deletes author + profile + books + reviews of those books; **BUT** tags remain.

**Mandatory verifications:**
- Grep the SQL log for `POST /authors/:id/profile`: there is **one INSERT INTO author_profiles** triggered by cascade (no manual `profileRepo.save`).
- Try `POST /books` twice with the same `metadata.isbn` -> second insert fails with `23505 duplicate key value violates unique constraint "uniq_book_isbn"`; two books without `isbn` (`isbn IS NULL`) **both succeed** (proves partial index).
- `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) SELECT * FROM books WHERE search_vector @@ to_tsquery('english', 'nestjs');` shows `Bitmap Index Scan on idx_book_search_vector`.
- `created_at` and `updated_at` of a book: after `PATCH /books/:id`, `updated_at` changes and `created_at` does not; verify via SQL `UPDATE ... RETURNING` in log or by querying the DB before/after.
- `DELETE /authors/:id` performs four things (delete author, profile, books, reviews) in the right cascade order; no FK violation thrown.

**Forbidden:**
- `synchronize: true` -> **0 prompt migration** (carry over from EASY).
- Using `@Column({ type: 'json' })` instead of `'jsonb'` -> **0 prompt jsonb** (json = plaintext, jsonb = binary + indexable - different natures).
- Calling `profileRepo.save()` / `reviewRepo.save()` manually instead of going through cascade via `authorRepo.save(author)` / `bookRepo.save(book)` in the create profile / nested review endpoint -> **0 prompt cascade**.
- Updating `search_vector` in TypeScript instead of via DB trigger -> **0 prompt GIN index** (breaks consistency for raw SQL writes outside app).
- Using `new Date()` manually for `createdAt` / `updatedAt` -> **0 prompt auto timestamp**.
challenges.prerequisites:
- Finished EASY `0-library-author-book-tag-crud-easy`.
- Basic Postgres knowledge: jsonb operators (`->`, `->>`, `@>`), tsvector/tsquery, PL/pgSQL triggers.
- Understand cascade semantics (save cascade vs onDelete cascade - they are different).

translations.value: TypeORM nâng cao - index chiến lược, jsonb column, quan hệ 1-1/1-n/n-n với cascade và auto timestamp

Nâng project library-typeorm-postgres (EASY) lên mức hands-on TypeORM - tập trung vào các feature thư viện mà dev production phải nắm: (1) index đủ 4 kiểu - single-column, composite, unique partial, GIN cho full-text search; (2) jsonb column trên Postgres (không phải BSON của Mongo - TypeORM map qua type jsonb cho structured binary JSON) để lưu Book.metadata kiểu schema lỏng, query được bằng operator -> và @>; (3) quan hệ đầy đủ: Author 1-1 AuthorProfile (shared PK), Author 1-n Book, Book 1-n Review, Book n-n Tag; (4) cascade đúng chỗ - save cascade cho profile/reviews/tags, onDelete CASCADE cho profile/reviews nhưng RESTRICT cho tag (không được xóa tag theo book); (5) auto timestamp @CreateDateColumn + @UpdateDateColumn + @DeleteDateColumn với default DB-side và entity hook @BeforeUpdate ghi version thủ công để verify hoạt động.

Fork project EASY sang `library-typeorm-advanced-features`. Mở rộng:

**Entity mới / sửa:**
- **`AuthorProfile`** (1-1 với `Author` qua **shared PK**):
  - `id` UUID PK đồng thời là FK đến `authors.id` (dùng `@OneToOne` + `@JoinColumn` + `@PrimaryColumn`).
  - `avatarUrl` varchar.
  - `social` jsonb `{ twitter?: string, github?: string, website?: string }`.
  - `stats` jsonb `{ totalBooks: number, totalReviews: number, avgRating: number }` (read-mostly, được recompute bởi service).
  - `@CreateDateColumn`, `@UpdateDateColumn`.
- **`Review`** (1-n từ `Book`):
  - `id` UUID PK.
  - `bookId` FK, quan hệ `@ManyToOne(() => Book, { onDelete: 'CASCADE' })`.
  - `reviewerName` varchar NOT NULL.
  - `rating` smallint CHECK `BETWEEN 1 AND 5`.
  - `comment` text nullable.
  - `@CreateDateColumn` (không cần updatedAt).
- **`Book` sửa**:
  - Thêm `@Column({ type: 'jsonb', default: {} }) metadata: { isbn?: string; pages?: number; language?: string; coverUrl?: string; }`.
  - Thêm `@Column({ type: 'tsvector', nullable: true, select: false }) searchVector: any;` - được trigger DB-side update khi `title` thay đổi (setup trong migration, KHÔNG app-side).
  - Quan hệ `@OneToMany(() => Review, (r) => r.book, { cascade: ['insert'] }) reviews: Review[];`.
  - Giữ `@ManyToMany(() => Tag, { cascade: ['insert'] })` - KHÔNG `onDelete: 'CASCADE'` trên pivot `book_tags` cho phía Tag (để tag sống độc lập).
- **`Author` sửa**:
  - Thêm `@OneToOne(() => AuthorProfile, (p) => p.author, { cascade: true, eager: false }) profile?: AuthorProfile;`.
  - Vẫn giữ `@OneToMany Book { onDelete: 'CASCADE' }` từ EASY.

**Index bắt buộc (khai báo qua decorator `@Index`, KHÔNG raw SQL rời rạc):**
- `@Index(['title'])` trên `Book` - B-tree lookup theo title.
- `@Index(['authorId', 'publishedYear'])` composite trên `Book` - filter "sách của author X trong năm Y".
- `@Index('uniq_book_isbn', { synchronize: true }, ...)` **unique partial index**: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uniq_book_isbn ON books ((metadata->>'isbn')) WHERE metadata->>'isbn' IS NOT NULL;` (dùng raw trong migration vì TypeORM decorator không cover partial).
- `@Index('idx_book_search_vector', { synchronize: false })` GIN: `CREATE INDEX idx_book_search_vector ON books USING GIN (search_vector);` (raw trong migration).
- `@Index(['rating'])` trên `Review` - sort/filter theo rating.
- `@Index(['bookId', 'rating'])` composite trên `Review` - query "top review của book".

**Migration:**
- `CreateAuthorProfile` - tạo bảng `author_profiles` với shared PK + FK CASCADE.
- `CreateReview` - tạo bảng `reviews` + FK CASCADE + CHECK rating + 2 index (rating, composite).
- `AddBookMetadataJsonb` - thêm `metadata jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb` + unique partial index `uniq_book_isbn`.
- `AddBookSearchVector` - thêm `search_vector tsvector` + trigger DB-side:
  ```sql
  CREATE FUNCTION books_search_trigger() RETURNS trigger AS $$
  BEGIN NEW.search_vector := to_tsvector('english', coalesce(NEW.title, '')); RETURN NEW; END;
  $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
  CREATE TRIGGER books_search_update BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF title ON books
    FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION books_search_trigger();
  CREATE INDEX idx_book_search_vector ON books USING GIN(search_vector);
  ```
- Tất cả migration có `up()` và `down()` đầy đủ.

**Endpoint mới:**
- `POST /authors/:id/profile` body `{ avatarUrl, social, stats? }` -> tạo profile cascade qua `authorRepo.save(author)` (KHÔNG insert trực tiếp `profileRepo`, để demo cascade).
- `GET /authors/:id?withProfile=true` -> eager load profile khi query param `withProfile=true`; mặc định không load (vì entity config `eager: false`).
- `POST /books/:id/reviews` body `{ reviewerName, rating, comment? }` -> 201. Validate `rating 1-5` qua `class-validator`. Sau insert, recompute `author.profile.stats` (totalReviews, avgRating) trong cùng transaction.
- `GET /books/search?q=<keyword>` -> dùng `to_tsquery` với GIN index:
  ```ts
  this.bookRepo.createQueryBuilder('book')
    .where(`book.search_vector @@ to_tsquery('english', :q)`, { q: keyword.split(' ').join(' & ') })
    .orderBy(`ts_rank(book.search_vector, to_tsquery('english', :q))`, 'DESC')
  ```
- `GET /books/by-isbn/:isbn` -> `WHERE metadata->>'isbn' = :isbn` (verify index unique partial được dùng qua `EXPLAIN`).
- `GET /books/by-language/:lang` -> `WHERE metadata->>'language' = :lang`.
- `POST /books` (đã có) cho phép nhận nguyên object `metadata` + mảng `reviews[]` nested - cascade insert 1 call tạo cả book + review.
- `DELETE /books/:id` -> cascade xóa `reviews`, KHÔNG xóa tag; các tag vẫn còn trong bảng `tags` (verify bằng count trước/sau).
- `DELETE /authors/:id` -> cascade xóa author + profile + books + reviews của các book đó; **NHƯNG** tag vẫn nguyên.

**Bắt buộc verify:**
- Grep log SQL của `POST /authors/:id/profile`: thấy **1 INSERT vào author_profiles** xảy ra do cascade (không phải gọi `profileRepo.save` thủ công).
- Thử gọi `POST /books` với 2 book cùng `metadata.isbn` -> insert thứ 2 fail `23505 duplicate key value violates unique constraint "uniq_book_isbn"`; trong khi 2 book không có `isbn` (`isbn IS NULL`) **vẫn insert được** cả 2 (chứng minh partial index).
- `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) SELECT * FROM books WHERE search_vector @@ to_tsquery('english', 'nestjs');` show `Bitmap Index Scan on idx_book_search_vector`.
- `created_at` và `updated_at` của book: sau `PATCH /books/:id`, `updated_at` thay đổi còn `created_at` giữ nguyên; verify trong log SQL `UPDATE` có `WHERE id = $N RETURNING ...` hoặc trực tiếp query DB trước/sau.
- `DELETE /authors/:id` làm 4 thứ (xóa author, profile, books, reviews) đúng thứ tự / cascade; không throw FK violation.

**Cấm:**
- `synchronize: true` -> **0 prompt migration** (giữ cấm từ EASY).
- Dùng `@Column({ type: 'json' })` thay vì `'jsonb'` -> **0 prompt jsonb** (json plaintext, jsonb binary + indexable - khác bản chất).
- Gọi `profileRepo.save()` / `reviewRepo.save()` thủ công thay vì cascade qua `authorRepo.save(author)` / `bookRepo.save(book)` ở endpoint tạo profile / bulk review -> **0 prompt cascade**.
- Update `search_vector` trong application code (TypeScript) thay vì trigger DB -> **0 prompt index GIN** (vì không đảm bảo consistency khi ghi bằng raw SQL ngoài app).
- Dùng `new Date()` thủ công cho `createdAt` / `updatedAt` -> **0 prompt auto timestamp**.

- Đã xong EASY `0-library-author-book-tag-crud-easy`.
- Biết cơ bản Postgres: jsonb operators (`->`, `->>`, `@>`), tsvector/tsquery, trigger PL/pgSQL.
- Hiểu cascade semantics (save cascade vs onDelete cascade - khác nhau).
Advanced TypeORM - index strategy, jsonb column, 1-1/1-n/n-n relations with cascade and auto timestamp

Upgrade the EASY project library-typeorm-postgres to a hands-on TypeORM level focused on library features every production dev must master: (1) indexes - single-column, composite, unique partial, GIN for full-text search; (2) jsonb column on Postgres (not Mongo's BSON - TypeORM maps it to the jsonb type for structured binary JSON) to store Book.metadata with a loose schema, queryable via operators -> and @>; (3) full relation coverage: Author 1-1 AuthorProfile (shared PK), Author 1-n Book, Book 1-n Review, Book n-n Tag; (4) cascade in the right places - save cascade for profile/reviews/tags, onDelete CASCADE for profile/reviews but RESTRICT for tag (tags must outlive books); (5) auto timestamps @CreateDateColumn + @UpdateDateColumn + @DeleteDateColumn with DB-side defaults and a @BeforeUpdate hook to prove it works.

Fork the EASY project to `library-typeorm-advanced-features`. Extend as follows:

**New / changed entities:**
- **`AuthorProfile`** (1-1 with `Author` via **shared PK**):
  - `id` UUID PK that is also FK to `authors.id` (use `@OneToOne` + `@JoinColumn` + `@PrimaryColumn`).
  - `avatarUrl` varchar.
  - `social` jsonb `{ twitter?: string, github?: string, website?: string }`.
  - `stats` jsonb `{ totalBooks: number, totalReviews: number, avgRating: number }` (read-mostly, recomputed by service).
  - `@CreateDateColumn`, `@UpdateDateColumn`.
- **`Review`** (1-n from `Book`):
  - `id` UUID PK.
  - `bookId` FK, relation `@ManyToOne(() => Book, { onDelete: 'CASCADE' })`.
  - `reviewerName` varchar NOT NULL.
  - `rating` smallint CHECK `BETWEEN 1 AND 5`.
  - `comment` text nullable.
  - `@CreateDateColumn` only (no updatedAt).
- **`Book` updated**:
  - Add `@Column({ type: 'jsonb', default: {} }) metadata: { isbn?: string; pages?: number; language?: string; coverUrl?: string; }`.
  - Add `@Column({ type: 'tsvector', nullable: true, select: false }) searchVector: any;` populated via a DB-side trigger when `title` changes (setup in migration, NOT in app).
  - Relation `@OneToMany(() => Review, (r) => r.book, { cascade: ['insert'] }) reviews: Review[];`.
  - Keep `@ManyToMany(() => Tag, { cascade: ['insert'] })` - DO NOT put `onDelete: 'CASCADE'` from the pivot `book_tags` to the Tag side (tags must remain).
- **`Author` updated**:
  - Add `@OneToOne(() => AuthorProfile, (p) => p.author, { cascade: true, eager: false }) profile?: AuthorProfile;`.
  - Keep EASY's `@OneToMany Book { onDelete: 'CASCADE' }`.

**Mandatory indexes (declare via `@Index` decorator, NO ad-hoc raw SQL floating around):**
- `@Index(['title'])` on `Book` - B-tree lookup by title.
- `@Index(['authorId', 'publishedYear'])` composite on `Book` - filter "books by author X in year Y".
- `@Index('uniq_book_isbn', ...)` **unique partial index**: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uniq_book_isbn ON books ((metadata->>'isbn')) WHERE metadata->>'isbn' IS NOT NULL;` (raw in migration because TypeORM decorator does not cover partial).
- `@Index('idx_book_search_vector', { synchronize: false })` GIN: `CREATE INDEX idx_book_search_vector ON books USING GIN (search_vector);` (raw in migration).
- `@Index(['rating'])` on `Review` - sort/filter by rating.
- `@Index(['bookId', 'rating'])` composite on `Review` - "top review per book".

**Migrations:**
- `CreateAuthorProfile` - creates `author_profiles` with shared PK + FK CASCADE.
- `CreateReview` - creates `reviews` + FK CASCADE + CHECK rating + 2 indexes (rating, composite).
- `AddBookMetadataJsonb` - adds `metadata jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb` + unique partial index `uniq_book_isbn`.
- `AddBookSearchVector` - adds `search_vector tsvector` + DB-side trigger:
  ```sql
  CREATE FUNCTION books_search_trigger() RETURNS trigger AS $$
  BEGIN NEW.search_vector := to_tsvector('english', coalesce(NEW.title, '')); RETURN NEW; END;
  $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
  CREATE TRIGGER books_search_update BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF title ON books
    FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION books_search_trigger();
  CREATE INDEX idx_book_search_vector ON books USING GIN(search_vector);
  ```
- Every migration must implement full `up()` and `down()`.

**New endpoints:**
- `POST /authors/:id/profile` body `{ avatarUrl, social, stats? }` -> cascade create via `authorRepo.save(author)` (NOT `profileRepo.save` directly - to demo cascade).
- `GET /authors/:id?withProfile=true` -> eager load profile when the query param is present; default does not load (entity is `eager: false`).
- `POST /books/:id/reviews` body `{ reviewerName, rating, comment? }` -> 201. Validate `rating 1-5` via `class-validator`. After insert, recompute `author.profile.stats` (totalReviews, avgRating) in the same transaction.
- `GET /books/search?q=<keyword>` -> full-text search via GIN index:
  ```ts
  this.bookRepo.createQueryBuilder('book')
    .where(`book.search_vector @@ to_tsquery('english', :q)`, { q: keyword.split(' ').join(' & ') })
    .orderBy(`ts_rank(book.search_vector, to_tsquery('english', :q))`, 'DESC')
  ```
- `GET /books/by-isbn/:isbn` -> `WHERE metadata->>'isbn' = :isbn` (verify unique partial index is used via `EXPLAIN`).
- `GET /books/by-language/:lang` -> `WHERE metadata->>'language' = :lang`.
- `POST /books` (already exists) accepts a full `metadata` object + nested `reviews[]` - cascade insert book + reviews in a single call.
- `DELETE /books/:id` -> cascade deletes `reviews`, does NOT delete tags; tags remain in the `tags` table (verify by count before/after).
- `DELETE /authors/:id` -> cascade deletes author + profile + books + reviews of those books; **BUT** tags remain.

**Mandatory verifications:**
- Grep the SQL log for `POST /authors/:id/profile`: there is **one INSERT INTO author_profiles** triggered by cascade (no manual `profileRepo.save`).
- Try `POST /books` twice with the same `metadata.isbn` -> second insert fails with `23505 duplicate key value violates unique constraint "uniq_book_isbn"`; two books without `isbn` (`isbn IS NULL`) **both succeed** (proves partial index).
- `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) SELECT * FROM books WHERE search_vector @@ to_tsquery('english', 'nestjs');` shows `Bitmap Index Scan on idx_book_search_vector`.
- `created_at` and `updated_at` of a book: after `PATCH /books/:id`, `updated_at` changes and `created_at` does not; verify via SQL `UPDATE ... RETURNING` in log or by querying the DB before/after.
- `DELETE /authors/:id` performs four things (delete author, profile, books, reviews) in the right cascade order; no FK violation thrown.

**Forbidden:**
- `synchronize: true` -> **0 prompt migration** (carry over from EASY).
- Using `@Column({ type: 'json' })` instead of `'jsonb'` -> **0 prompt jsonb** (json = plaintext, jsonb = binary + indexable - different natures).
- Calling `profileRepo.save()` / `reviewRepo.save()` manually instead of going through cascade via `authorRepo.save(author)` / `bookRepo.save(book)` in the create profile / nested review endpoint -> **0 prompt cascade**.
- Updating `search_vector` in TypeScript instead of via DB trigger -> **0 prompt GIN index** (breaks consistency for raw SQL writes outside app).
- Using `new Date()` manually for `createdAt` / `updatedAt` -> **0 prompt auto timestamp**.

- Finished EASY `0-library-author-book-tag-crud-easy`.
- Basic Postgres knowledge: jsonb operators (`->`, `->>`, `@>`), tsvector/tsquery, PL/pgSQL triggers.
- Understand cascade semantics (save cascade vs onDelete cascade - they are different).

steps.title: Fork EASY, install deps, scaffold new entities
steps.body:
**Steps**
- **Step 1:** Copy EASY to `library-typeorm-advanced-features`, keep the 3 entities + 2 migrations.
- **Step 2:** Install extra deps (if missing):
  ```bash
  npm i class-validator class-transformer
  ```
- **Step 3:** Generate module + service + controller:
  ```bash
  nest g module review
  nest g controller review
  nest g service review
  nest g module profile
  nest g service profile
  ```
- **Step 4:** Create `src/author/entities/author-profile.entity.ts` and `src/review/entities/review.entity.ts` (empty shells for now).

**Minimum acceptance criteria**
- New project folder `library-typeorm-advanced-features` boots with `npm run start:dev`.
- `package.json` contains `class-validator` and `class-transformer`.
- New modules `ReviewModule` and `ProfileModule` exist and are imported into `AppModule`.
- Original 3 entities + 2 EASY migrations remain; `synchronize: false` unchanged.

**Nice to have**
- Add Swagger `@nestjs/swagger` with `/api` endpoint to verify schema after each step.
- Set `strictPropertyInitialization: false` in `tsconfig.json` if TypeScript complains about uninitialized entity fields.
