steps.title: Auto timestamp + @BeforeInsert / @BeforeUpdate hook and smoke test 5 scenarios
steps.body:
**Steps**
- **Step 1:** Verify auto timestamps from EASY: `@CreateDateColumn() createdAt: Date;` and `@UpdateDateColumn() updatedAt: Date;` on `Author`, `Book` (and `Review` createdAt only, `AuthorProfile` has both). Ensure NO manual `new Date()` assigns those fields anywhere in services - grep the entire repo.
- **Step 2:** Add `@BeforeUpdate` hook on `Book` demonstrating an additional side effect (e.g. normalize `title.trim()`):
  ```ts
  @BeforeInsert() @BeforeUpdate()
  trimTitle() {
    if (this.title) this.title = this.title.trim();
  }
  ```
  (This hook only runs when using `repo.save(entity)`, NOT `repo.update(id, partial)` - document it in the README.)
- **Step 3:** Run smoke test. `docker compose up -d`, `npm run migration:run`, `npm run start:dev`.
- **Step 4:** Cascade save profile:

  **API title:** **Author API - create profile via cascade - POST http://localhost:3000/authors/<authorId>/profile**

  **How to call:** Use Postman to `POST` `http://localhost:3000/authors/<authorId>/profile`, tab `Body` -> `raw` -> `JSON`.

  **JSON body:** `{"avatarUrl":"https://cdn/a.png","social":{"github":"orwell"}}`

  Or using **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/authors/<authorId>/profile \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"avatarUrl":"https://cdn/a.png","social":{"github":"orwell"}}' -i
  ```
- **Step 5:** Nested create book + reviews + metadata:

  **API title:** **Book API - create book with reviews and metadata - POST http://localhost:3000/books**

  **How to call:** Use Postman to `POST` `http://localhost:3000/books`, tab `Body` -> `raw` -> `JSON`.

  **JSON body:** `{"title":"Advanced NestJS","authorId":"<a>","tagIds":["<t>"],"metadata":{"isbn":"978-1","pages":300,"language":"en"},"reviews":[{"reviewerName":"Alice","rating":5,"comment":"Great"},{"reviewerName":"Bob","rating":4}]}`

  Or using **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/books \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"title":"Advanced NestJS","authorId":"<a>","tagIds":["<t>"],"metadata":{"isbn":"978-1","pages":300,"language":"en"},"reviews":[{"reviewerName":"Alice","rating":5,"comment":"Great"},{"reviewerName":"Bob","rating":4}]}' -i
  ```
- **Step 6:** Duplicate isbn fail:

  **API title:** **Book API - duplicate isbn - POST http://localhost:3000/books**

  **How to call:** Use Postman to `POST` `http://localhost:3000/books`, reuse the same `isbn`.

  **JSON body:** `{"title":"Duplicate","authorId":"<a>","tagIds":["<t>"],"metadata":{"isbn":"978-1"}}`

  Or using **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/books \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"title":"Duplicate","authorId":"<a>","tagIds":["<t>"],"metadata":{"isbn":"978-1"}}' -i
  ```
  Expect HTTP 409 or 500, response mentions `23505` or `uniq_book_isbn`.
- **Step 7:** Full-text search:

  **API title:** **Book API - full text search - GET http://localhost:3000/books/search?q=nestjs**

  **How to call:** Use Postman to `GET` `http://localhost:3000/books/search?q=nestjs`.

  **JSON body:** No body for a `GET` request.

  Or using **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl "http://localhost:3000/books/search?q=nestjs" -i
  ```
- **Step 8:** Auto updatedAt:

  **API title:** **Book API - patch title and observe updatedAt - PATCH http://localhost:3000/books/<bookId>**

  **How to call:** Use Postman to `PATCH` `http://localhost:3000/books/<bookId>`, tab `Body` -> `raw` -> `JSON`.

  **JSON body:** `{"title":"Advanced NestJS v2"}`

  Or using **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl -X PATCH http://localhost:3000/books/<bookId> \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"title":"Advanced NestJS v2"}' -i
  ```
  Then query the DB before/after to compare `createdAt` (unchanged) and `updatedAt` (changed), and `SELECT search_vector FROM books` to see it reindexed with the new title.
- **Step 9:** In `README.md` under **Smoke Test**, paste:
  - Responses from the 5 scenarios (cascade profile, create book nested, duplicate isbn, search, patch).
  - `\di` listing showing all 6 indexes (2 single, 2 composite, 1 unique partial, 1 GIN).
  - `\d author_profiles`, `\d reviews`, `\d books` showing columns + FKs + CHECKs.
  - `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` of `GET /books/search?q=nestjs` showing `Bitmap Index Scan on idx_book_search_vector`.

**Minimum acceptance criteria**
- The 5 smoke test scenarios all produce the expected results above; responses/errors pasted verbatim into README.
- Grep the entire repo: NO `new Date()` assigned to `createdAt` or `updatedAt` in any service.
- All 4 new migrations (profile, review, metadata+isbn, search_vector+trigger) run and revert cleanly; running `npm run migration:revert` 4 times restores the DB to the EASY state.
- `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` of the search endpoint is pasted into README with plan `Bitmap Index Scan on idx_book_search_vector`.
- `\di` output in README shows **at least 6 indexes** between `books` and `reviews` (title, author_id+published_year, uniq_book_isbn, idx_book_search_vector, rating, book_id+rating).

**Nice to have**
- Write `docs/TIMELINE.md` summarizing the migration order and what each migration adds, so newcomers can follow.
- Micro-benchmark with `autocannon` comparing search/by-isbn/by-language endpoints with vs without their indexes.
- Export a Postman Collection covering all 5 smoke test scenarios.

challenges.title: Loan feature with transaction, optimistic lock, index strategy, and before/after EXPLAIN ANALYZE
challenges.description: A production-grade problem: extend library-typeorm-advanced-config (MEDIUM) with a real loan feature - (1) an ACID transaction for the borrow flow: decrement Book.stock, insert a Loan record atomically, rollback on stock <= 0; (2) an optimistic lock via @VersionColumn on Book to detect concurrent updates + a retry handler with exponential backoff (max 3 attempts) then a 409 Conflict; (3) an index strategy for GET /users/:id/loans?status=BORROWED - detect N+1 yourself, add a composite (userid, status) index + a partial index WHERE status='BORROWED', run EXPLAIN ANALYZE before and after indexing, and paste the outputs into the README with an Execution Time comparison. The concurrent test is mandatory: 10 users hit borrow on the same book (stock=5) through Promise.all -> exactly 5 succeed, 5 fail with 409, final stock = 0, no double-spend.
challenges.requirements:
Fork MEDIUM into `library-loan-optimistic-lock`. Additions:
- **Entity `User`** (`id` UUID PK, `email` UNIQUE, `name`, `createdAt`). Kept minimal - no real auth.
- **Column `Book.stock`** int NOT NULL default 0 (migration `AddBookStock`).
- **Column `Book.version`** int managed by `@VersionColumn()` (migration `AddBookVersion`).
- **Entity `Loan`**:
  - `id` UUID, `userId` FK, `bookId` FK, `borrowedAt` timestamp NOT NULL default now, `returnedAt` timestamp NULL, `status` enum (`BORROWED` | `RETURNED`).
  - `@ManyToOne User { onDelete: 'CASCADE' }`, `@ManyToOne Book { onDelete: 'RESTRICT' }`.
  - Migration `CreateLoans` creates the `loans` table with 3 indexes: `idx_loans_book_id`, `idx_loans_user_id_status` (composite), `idx_loans_borrowed_at` (BRIN or B-tree).
- **`POST /loans/borrow`** body `{ userId, bookId }`:
  - Use `DataSource.transaction(async (em) => {...})` (the manager-style transaction - avoid manual `QueryRunner` unless you genuinely need explicit commit/rollback control).
  - Inside the transaction: `findOneBy({ id: bookId })` to load the version, check `stock > 0`, `stock -= 1`, `em.save(book)` (TypeORM automatically appends `WHERE version = :v` when saving an entity with a version - **verify** in the SQL log), then `em.save(Loan, {...})`.
  - If TypeORM throws `OptimisticLockVersionMismatchError` -> a **retry handler** with exponential backoff `100ms, 200ms, 400ms` (max 3 attempts). After 3 failures -> throw `ConflictException` HTTP 409 with body `{ code: 'CONCURRENT_CONFLICT', message: ... }`.
  - If `stock <= 0` -> `ConflictException` HTTP 409 `{ code: 'OUT_OF_STOCK', ... }`.
  - If `book` does not exist -> 404 `{ code: 'BOOK_NOT_FOUND' }`.
- **`POST /loans/:id/return`**: transaction that sets `status='RETURNED'`, `returnedAt=now()`, `stock += 1`. Idempotent: calling it again when already `RETURNED` returns 409 `{ code: 'ALREADY_RETURNED' }`.
- **`GET /users/:id/loans?status=BORROWED`** via `QueryBuilder` with `leftJoinAndSelect('loan.book', 'book')` + `leftJoinAndSelect('book.author', 'author')` to defeat N+1. Verify via SQL log: **exactly 1 query** (not 1 + N).
- **Benchmark script** `scripts/benchmark-concurrency.ts` using `Promise.all` to fire 10 users borrowing the same book (stock=5), logging `{ok: 5, conflict: 5, finalStock: 0}`. Runnable via `npm run bench:concurrency`.
- **README section EXPLAIN ANALYZE**:

  - Quan hệ `@ManyToOne User { onDelete: 'CASCADE' }`, `@ManyToOne Book { onDelete: 'RESTRICT' }`.

SET stock = stock - 1 WHERE id=$1 AND stock > 0` (dù đúng về mặt nghiệp vụ nhưng không demo được optimistic lock) -> **0 prompt optimistic lock**. Nếu muốn dùng atomic update đó, phải dùng **cùng lúc với** optimistic lock để chứng minh hiểu.

steps.title: Fix N+1 on GET /users/:id/loans and verify via query count
steps.body:
**Steps to follow**
- **Step 1:** Temporarily write a naive **wrong** version in the branch `bad-n-plus-1`:
  ```ts
  const loans = await this.loanRepo.find({ where: { userId } });
  for (const l of loans) {
    l.book = await this.bookRepo.findOneBy({ id: l.bookId });
    l.book.author = await this.authorRepo.findOneBy({ id: l.book.authorId });
  }
  ```
  Hit `GET /users/:id/loans` on 20 loans -> inspect SQL log: expect **41 queries** (1 loans + 20 books + 20 authors).
- **Step 2:** Merge into `main` with the correct fix using `QueryBuilder`:
  ```ts
  return this.dataSource.getRepository(Loan)
    .createQueryBuilder('loan')
    .leftJoinAndSelect('loan.book', 'book')
    .leftJoinAndSelect('book.author', 'author')
    .where('loan.userId = :userId', { userId })
    .andWhere(status ? 'loan.status = :status' : '1=1', { status })
    .orderBy('loan.borrowedAt', 'DESC')
    .getMany();
  ```
- **Step 3:** Verify the SQL log: `GET /users/:id/loans` produces **exactly one SELECT** with `LEFT JOIN books` and `LEFT JOIN authors`.
- **Step 4:** Write an e2e test (`supertest` + a spy on `WinstonQueryLogger.logQuery`) that asserts query count <= 2 (allowing 1 warmup + 1 real).
- **Step 5:** Under **N+1 Fix** in the README, paste:
  - A screenshot of the SQL log running the wrong version (query count visible).
  - A screenshot of the SQL log running the correct version (1 query).
  - A short code diff.

**Minimum acceptance criteria**
- `GET /users/:id/loans` with 20 loans produces a **single** SELECT with `LEFT JOIN` (verified by TypeORM log; grep `SELECT "loan"` matches once).
- The e2e test `loans.e2e-spec.ts` asserts `queryCount <= 2` for that endpoint.
- The response contains both `loan.book.title` and `loan.book.author.name` (two-level nesting), no `undefined`.
- The README **N+1 Fix** section contains before/after screenshots.

**Nice to have**
- Use the `dataloader` pattern for use cases where you don't want a huge JOIN (batch-loading authors).
- Benchmark: hit the endpoint 100 times via `autocannon` and compare latency before/after in the README.

steps.title: Seed 50k loans + EXPLAIN ANALYZE before/after the composite + partial indexes
steps.body:
**Steps to follow**
- **Step 1:** Write `scripts/seed-big.ts` inserting **>= 50k loans**, 100 users, 500 books (random `user_id`, `book_id`, `status` 70% BORROWED / 30% RETURNED). Use `queryRunner.manager.createQueryBuilder().insert()` batching 1000 rows at a time; keep `synchronize:false`.
  ```bash
  npm run db:seed:big
  ```
- **Step 2:** Before adding the composite index, run `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`:
  ```bash
  docker exec -it <pg> psql -U library -d library -c \
    "EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) SELECT * FROM loans WHERE user_id = '<user>' AND status = 'BORROWED';"
  ```
  Paste the output into the README under **EXPLAIN ANALYZE - Before**. Expect `Seq Scan on loans` or a slow `Bitmap Index Scan` with `Execution Time` > 30ms.
- **Step 3:** Create a new migration `AddLoansIndex`:
  ```ts
  await queryRunner.query(`CREATE INDEX idx_loans_user_id_status ON loans(user_id, status);`);
  await queryRunner.query(`CREATE INDEX idx_loans_borrowed_partial ON loans(user_id, borrowed_at) WHERE status='BORROWED';`);
  ```
  `down()` drops both indexes.
  ```bash
  npm run migration:run
  ```
- **Step 4:** Run `VACUUM ANALYZE loans;` to refresh planner statistics:
  ```bash
  docker exec -it <pg> psql -U library -d library -c "VACUUM ANALYZE loans;"
  ```
- **Step 5:** Re-run the `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` from Step 2. Paste the output under **EXPLAIN ANALYZE - After**. Expect `Index Scan using idx_loans_user_id_status` with `Execution Time` down >= 5x.
- **Step 6:** Add the comparison table to the README:
  ```
  | Query            | Plan       | Execution Time | Shared Buffers |
  | Before index     | Seq Scan   | 45.2 ms        | 1234           |
  | After composite  | Index Scan | 0.8 ms         | 12             |
  ```

**Minimum acceptance criteria**
- `scripts/seed-big.ts` inserts **>= 50k loans** (verify via `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM loans;` >= 50000).
- Both EXPLAIN ANALYZE outputs (Before + After) are pasted **verbatim** (including `cost=...`, `Execution Time: ...ms`) in the README.
- Plan Before shows `Seq Scan on loans` or doesn't use the new index; Plan After shows `Index Scan using idx_loans_user_id_status` (or the partial `idx_loans_borrowed_partial`).
- `Execution Time` After / Before <= 0.2 (>= 5x speedup). Otherwise, document the reason in the README with a `BUFFERS` analysis - in which case this prompt fails.
- `AddLoansIndex` migration has an `up()` creating 2 indexes and a `down()` dropping both. `npm run migration:revert` removes both.

**Nice to have**
- Add `idx_loans_book_id_borrowed_at` to serve the "who borrowed book X" query.
- Inspect `pg_stat_user_indexes` after smoke tests to confirm `idx_scan` > 0.
- Further optimize with a **covering index** `CREATE INDEX ... INCLUDE (returned_at)` for index-only scans; remeasure Execution Time.

steps.title: Smoke-test 3 scenarios via Postman/curl and paste into the README
steps.body:
**Steps to follow**
- **Step 1:** Run `docker compose up -d`, `npm run migration:run`, `npm run db:seed`, `npm run start:dev`.
- **Step 2:** Test the happy borrow:

  **API name:** **Loan API - happy borrow - POST http://localhost:3000/loans/borrow**

  **How to call:** Use Postman to send `POST` to `http://localhost:3000/loans/borrow`, in the `Body` tab pick `raw` -> `JSON`.

  **JSON Body:** `{"userId":"<userId>","bookId":"<bookId-stock-3>"}`

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/loans/borrow \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"userId":"<userId>","bookId":"<bookId-stock-3>"}' -i
  ```
- **Step 3:** Test out-of-stock:

  **API name:** **Loan API - out of stock - POST http://localhost:3000/loans/borrow**

  **How to call:** Use Postman to send `POST` to `http://localhost:3000/loans/borrow`, in the `Body` tab pick `raw` -> `JSON`. Use a `bookId` with `stock=0`.

  **JSON Body:** `{"userId":"<userId>","bookId":"<bookId-stock-0>"}`

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/loans/borrow \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"userId":"<userId>","bookId":"<bookId-stock-0>"}' -i
  ```
  Expect 409 with body containing `"code":"OUT_OF_STOCK"`.
- **Step 4:** Test the N+1 fix:

  **API name:** **Loan API - list borrowed by user - GET http://localhost:3000/users/<userId>/loans?status=BORROWED**

  **How to call:** Use Postman to send `GET` to `http://localhost:3000/users/<userId>/loans?status=BORROWED`.

  **JSON Body:** No body for `GET` requests.

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl "http://localhost:3000/users/<userId>/loans?status=BORROWED" -i
  ```
  Screenshot the SQL log showing **exactly one SELECT**.
- **Step 5:** Run the concurrent script:
  ```bash
  npm run bench:concurrency
  ```
  Confirm output `{ ok: 5, conflict: 5, finalStock: 0 }`. Run 5 consecutive times (resetting `stock=5` between runs via seed).
- **Step 6:** In the README **Smoke Test** section, paste:
  - The happy-borrow response (the `Book` in it has `version: 2`).
  - The out-of-stock 409 response.
  - The SQL log screenshot for `GET /users/:id/loans?status=BORROWED` (one query).
  - Terminal output across 5 concurrent runs (5x `{ok:5, conflict:5, finalStock:0}`).
  - The EXPLAIN ANALYZE Before/After block (already pasted in Step 4 Step 4).

**Minimum acceptance criteria**
- The happy-borrow response shows the `Book` object with a `version` greater than before the borrow.
- The out-of-stock 409 JSON contains `"code":"OUT_OF_STOCK"`.
- The SQL log for `GET /users/:id/loans?status=BORROWED` contains **exactly one** SELECT line.
- The concurrent script reports `ok=5, conflict=5, finalStock=0` on all 5 runs.
- The README contains all 5 pieces of evidence (happy response, out-of-stock response, 1-query screenshot, 5x concurrent output, EXPLAIN ANALYZE Before/After block).

**Nice to have**
- Benchmark with `autocannon -c 50 -d 30 http://localhost:3000/users/<id>/loans?status=BORROWED`, paste p99.
- Add a scenario for return + an immediate borrow of the same book by a different user to exercise the return-re-opens-stock flow.

prompts.title: ACID transaction for borrow + return, correct rollback on out-of-stock or version mismatch
prompts.promptText: `LoanService.borrow` and `LoanService.return` run inside `dataSource.transaction(...)`. Borrow on `stock=0` -> 409 `OUT_OF_STOCK` with DB unchanged (stock stays 0, no new loan). Return called twice on the same `loanId` -> 409 `ALREADY_RETURNED` with stock not incremented again. Every stock-related write sits inside a transaction; repo-wide grep finds no `bookRepo.save(book)` that changes stock outside one.

`LoanService.borrow` và `LoanService.return` đều chạy trong `dataSource.transaction(...)`. Borrow trên book `stock=0` -> 409 `OUT_OF_STOCK`, DB **không** thay đổi (stock vẫn 0, không có loan mới). Return lần 2 trên cùng `loanId` -> 409 `ALREADY_RETURNED`, stock không tăng thêm. Tất cả write liên quan stock đều nằm trong transaction; grep repo không thấy `bookRepo.save(book)` cho trường hợp stock ngoài transaction.

prompts.title: Optimistic lock via @VersionColumn + retry handler with exponential backoff (max 3)
prompts.promptText: `Book` carries `@VersionColumn() version: number`; the SQL log `UPDATE "books" ... WHERE "id"=$N AND "version"=$M` proves TypeORM uses real locking. The helper `retryOnOptimisticLock(fn, 3, 100)` retries on `OptimisticLockVersionMismatchError` with `100ms/200ms/400ms` delays; after 3 misses -> `ConflictException({code:'CONCURRENT_CONFLICT'})`. The concurrent test `Promise.all` for 10 users / stock=5, run 5 times, produces `ok=5, conflict=5, finalStock=0` every time, and the log shows at least one retry (never all passing on first try).

contents.title: NoSQL Storage with MongoDB and Mongoose
contents.description: Learn how to use Mongoose ODM in NestJS to define schemas, create indexes, manage timestamps, and work with MongoDB documents in a disciplined way.
contents.body:
## I. Introduction

When working with **MongoDB**, many beginners assume NoSQL means total freedom: no schema and no constraints. As systems grow, that assumption quickly leads to inconsistent data: a field exists in one document but is missing in another, and data types drift over time.

**Mongoose** solves this by adding an application-layer discipline. It enforces a defined **Schema** before documents are persisted, so you keep MongoDB flexibility without sacrificing data consistency.

## II. Essence

This lesson follows a **source-first** approach: read the Mongoose schema and service first, then test the API to see how MongoDB remains flexible while still guarded by validation and schema rules.

Clone [here](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/tree/main/fullstack-mastery/mongoose-and-mongodb)

### Runtime Dependency Diagram

```mermaid
graph LR
    Client((Client))
    Client --> CatsController[CatsController]
    CatsController --> CatsService[CatsService]
    CatsService --> CatModel[Mongoose Model<CatDocument>]
    CatModel --> CatSchema[CatSchema + indexes + timestamps]
    CatModel --> MDB[(MongoDB)]
```

### Source Code Tree (file-level)

```mermaid
treeView-beta
    "src"
        "app.module.ts"
        "modules"
            "cats"
                "cats.module.ts"
                "cats.controller.ts"
                "cats.service.ts"
                "schemas"
                    "cat.schema.ts"
                "dto"
                    "create-cat.dto.ts"
                    "update-cat.dto.ts"
```

### Environment Setup and Run Flow

- **1. Prerequisites:** `Node.js LTS`, `npm`, Docker Desktop, and Git are required.
- **2. Clone the demo source:** Clone/pull the source so your code context matches:
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources.git
  cd resources/fullstack-mastery/mongoose-and-mongodb
  git pull origin main
  ```
- **3. Start MongoDB:** Run the MongoDB container:
  ```bash
  docker compose -f .docker/mongodb.yaml up --build -d
  ```
- **4. Install dependencies and run the app:** Install packages and start the server:
  ```bash
  npm install
  npm run start:dev
  ```
- **5. Success signal:** The app runs on port `3000`; newly created documents include `createdAt` and `updatedAt`.

### Application Testing

- **Step 1:** Create a cat document with flexible metadata.

  **API Title:** **Cats API - create document - POST http://localhost:3000/cats**

  **How to call API:** Use Postman to send a `POST` request to `http://localhost:3000/cats`.

  **Body JSON:**
  ```json
  {
    "name": "Tom",
    "age": 3,
    "metadata": { "color": "orange", "weight": 4.5 },
    "hobbies": ["sleeping", "playing"]
  }
  ```

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/cats \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"name":"Tom","age":3,"metadata":{"color":"orange","weight":4.5},"hobbies":["sleeping","playing"]}'
  ```

- **Step 2:** Update a document by id and observe how `updatedAt` changes.

  **API Title:** **Cats API - patch cat age - PATCH http://localhost:3000/cats/{id}**

  **How to call API:** Use Postman to send a `PATCH` request to `http://localhost:3000/cats/{id}`.

  **Body JSON:**
  ```json
  {
    "age": 4
  }
  ```

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl -X PATCH http://localhost:3000/cats/REPLACE_ID \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"age":4}'
  ```

  **Trace code execution (by file):**
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts:21`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/mongoose-and-mongodb/src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts#L21) -> `CatsController.create()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:18`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/mongoose-and-mongodb/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L18) -> `CatsService.create()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/schemas/cat.schema.ts:9`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/mongoose-and-mongodb/src/modules/cats/schemas/cat.schema.ts#L9) -> `CatSchema` (`required`, `index`, `timestamps`)
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:41`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/mongoose-and-mongodb/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L41) -> `CatsService.update()`

  *Expected result:* Data is stored as flexible documents while validation enforces minimum consistency for critical fields.

## III. Core Concepts

### 1. ***Schema Discipline***

- **Role:** Mongoose schemas define a minimum data contract before documents are written.
- **Common mistake:** Assuming NoSQL means skipping validation entirely.
- **Production impact:** Inconsistent structures make querying and migration difficult.

### 2. ***MongoDB Indexing***

- **Role:** Indexes speed up queries on frequently filtered fields.
- **Common mistake:** Skipping indexes on hot fields like `name`, `email`, or `slug`.
- **Production impact:** Full collection scans and high latency at scale.

### 3. ***Flexible Fields***

- **Role:** `Object` and `Array` fields support flexible metadata/hobby storage without frequent migrations.
- **Common mistake:** Overusing free-form fields without an API contract.
- **Production impact:** Frontend/backend expectation mismatches and serialization bugs.

### 4. ***Query API and `.exec()`***

- **Role:** `.exec()` returns explicit Promises, making async flow and error handling clearer.
- **Common mistake:** Mixing callbacks, query objects, and `await` inconsistently.
- **Production impact:** Unpredictable error flow and difficult runtime tracing.

## IV. Advanced Techniques

For larger systems, combine schema validation with stronger patterns: add compound indexes for common filter/sort combinations, use partial indexes for sparse fields, and define DTO-level contracts that align with flexible document fields. This keeps read performance predictable while preserving MongoDB agility.

**Conclusion:** MongoDB is powerful not because it ignores schema, but because it allows flexible storage while Mongoose enforces discipline at the application boundary.

## V. Interview Questions

1. **Interview Question:**  
   "Why use Mongoose schemas in production even when using MongoDB?"
   - **What is being assessed:** Understanding the trade-off between flexibility and data discipline.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Explain that schemas enforce validation, standardize fields, reduce dirty data, and stabilize API behavior.

2. **Interview Question:**  
   "What value does `timestamps: true` provide in debugging and data auditing?"
   - **What is being assessed:** Observability and incident analysis mindset.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Use `createdAt/updatedAt` to trace changes, detect stale records, and investigate abnormal updates.

3. **Interview Question:**  
   "When should you store a list as an embedded array versus a separate collection?"
   - **What is being assessed:** MongoDB data modeling by access pattern.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Embed when data is read together and bounded in size; split when growth or independent querying becomes significant.

translations.value: Lưu trữ NoSQL với MongoDB và Mongoose
Tìm hiểu cách sử dụng Mongoose ODM để định nghĩa Schema, thiết lập index, sử dụng timestamps và thao tác dữ liệu với MongoDB trong NestJS.

## I. Lời mở đầu

Khi làm việc với **MongoDB**, nhiều lập trình viên mới bắt đầu thường nghĩ rằng "NoSQL là tự do tuyệt đối — không cần schema, không cần ràng buộc". Nhưng khi dự án lớn dần, dữ liệu không nhất quán bắt đầu xuất hiện khắp nơi: trường này có ở document A nhưng mất tích ở document B, kiểu dữ liệu loạn xạ vì không ai kiểm soát.

**Mongoose** ra đời để giải quyết vấn đề này — nó đặt ra **lớp kỷ luật** ngay trên tầng ứng dụng, ép mọi document phải tuân theo **Schema** đã định nghĩa trước khi được ghi vào database. Bài học này sẽ giúp bạn hiểu cách tận dụng sự linh hoạt của MongoDB trong khi vẫn duy trì tính nhất quán dữ liệu.

## II. Bản chất

Bài này đi theo hướng **source-first**: đọc schema và service Mongoose trước, rồi test API để thấy cách MongoDB lưu document linh hoạt nhưng vẫn có kỷ luật qua validation/schema.

Clone tại [đây](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/tree/main/fullstack-mastery/mongoose-and-mongodb)

### Sơ đồ phụ thuộc runtime

```mermaid
graph LR
    Client((Client))
    Client --> CatsController[CatsController]
    CatsController --> CatsService[CatsService]
    CatsService --> CatModel[Mongoose Model<CatDocument>]
    CatModel --> CatSchema[CatSchema + indexes + timestamps]
    CatModel --> MDB[(MongoDB)]
```

### Sơ đồ cây source code (file-level)

```mermaid
treeView-beta
    "src"
        "app.module.ts"
        "modules"
            "cats"
                "cats.module.ts"
                "cats.controller.ts"
                "cats.service.ts"
                "schemas"
                    "cat.schema.ts"
                "dto"
                    "create-cat.dto.ts"
                    "update-cat.dto.ts"
```

### Chuẩn bị Môi trường và Luồng Cài đặt

- **1. Prerequisites:** Cần `Node.js LTS`, `npm`, Docker Desktop và git.
- **2. Clone source demo:** Clone/pull source để đọc đúng context code:
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources.git
  cd resources/fullstack-mastery/mongoose-and-mongodb
  git pull origin main
  ```
- **3. Khởi động MongoDB:** Chạy container MongoDB:
  ```bash
  docker compose -f .docker/mongodb.yaml up --build -d
  ```
- **4. Cài dependency và chạy app:** Cài package rồi chạy server:
  ```bash
  npm install
  npm run start:dev
  ```
- **5. Tín hiệu thành công:** App chạy cổng `3000`; tạo mới document trả về có `createdAt` và `updatedAt`.

### Kiểm thử ứng dụng

- **Bước 1:** Tạo document cat với metadata linh hoạt.

  **Tiêu đề API:** **Cats API - create document - POST http://localhost:3000/cats**

  **Hướng dẫn gọi API:** Dùng Postman gửi `POST` tới `http://localhost:3000/cats`.

  **Body JSON:**
  ```json
  {
    "name": "Tom",
    "age": 3,
    "metadata": { "color": "orange", "weight": 4.5 },
    "hobbies": ["sleeping", "playing"]
  }
  ```

  Hoặc dùng **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/cats \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"name":"Tom","age":3,"metadata":{"color":"orange","weight":4.5},"hobbies":["sleeping","playing"]}'
  ```

- **Bước 2:** Cập nhật document theo id để thấy `updatedAt` thay đổi.

  **Tiêu đề API:** **Cats API - patch cat age - PATCH http://localhost:3000/cats/{id}**

  **Hướng dẫn gọi API:** Dùng Postman gửi `PATCH` tới `http://localhost:3000/cats/{id}`.

  **Body JSON:**
  ```json
  {
    "age": 4
  }
  ```

  Hoặc dùng **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl -X PATCH http://localhost:3000/cats/REPLACE_ID \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"age":4}'
  ```

  **Trace code execution (theo file):**
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts:21`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/mongoose-and-mongodb/src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts#L21) -> `CatsController.create()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:18`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/mongoose-and-mongodb/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L18) -> `CatsService.create()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/schemas/cat.schema.ts:9`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/mongoose-and-mongodb/src/modules/cats/schemas/cat.schema.ts#L9) -> `CatSchema` (`required`, `index`, `timestamps`)
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:41`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/mongoose-and-mongodb/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L41) -> `CatsService.update()`

  *Kết quả mong đợi:* Dữ liệu được lưu dạng document linh hoạt, validation giữ tính nhất quán tối thiểu ở các trường quan trọng.

  *Kết luận:* MongoDB + Mongoose phù hợp bài toán schema biến động nhanh nhưng vẫn cần guardrail ở tầng ứng dụng.

## III. Các khái niệm cốt lõi

### 1. ***Schema Discipline***

- **Vai trò:** Mongoose schema tạo chuẩn dữ liệu tối thiểu trước khi ghi document.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Hiểu nhầm NoSQL là bỏ validation hoàn toàn.
- **Hậu quả production:** Dữ liệu lệch cấu trúc, khó query và khó migrate.

### 2. ***Index trong MongoDB***

- **Vai trò:** Tăng tốc truy vấn cho các field tìm kiếm thường xuyên.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Không tạo index cho field nóng như `name`, `email`, `slug`.
- **Hậu quả production:** Full collection scan, latency tăng mạnh khi dữ liệu lớn.

### 3. ***Flexible Fields***

- **Vai trò:** `Object` và `Array` giúp lưu metadata/hobbies linh hoạt không cần migration dày đặc.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Lạm dụng field tự do mà không có contract API.
- **Hậu quả production:** Frontend/backend lệch kỳ vọng dữ liệu, bug serialization.

### 4. ***Query API và `.exec()`***

- **Vai trò:** `.exec()` trả Promise rõ ràng, dễ quản trị async flow và error handling.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Trộn callback, query object và await không nhất quán.
- **Hậu quả production:** Luồng lỗi khó đoán, khó trace nguyên nhân runtime.

## IV. Kết luận

**Mongoose** mang lại sự cân bằng hoàn hảo giữa tính linh hoạt của **MongoDB** và tính kỷ luật của schema. Với khả năng định nghĩa **index**, **timestamps**, và lưu trữ dữ liệu dạng **Object** và **Array** trực tiếp trong document, Mongoose là lựa chọn lý tưởng cho các dự án cần tốc độ phát triển nhanh nhưng vẫn đảm bảo chất lượng dữ liệu.

**Kết luận:** Sức mạnh của MongoDB không phải là "không cần schema" — mà là khả năng lưu trữ dữ liệu linh hoạt trong khi vẫn được Mongoose bảo vệ bằng lớp validation nghiêm ngặt ở tầng ứng dụng.

## V. Các mẫu câu phỏng vấn

1. **Câu hỏi phỏng vấn:**  
   “Tại sao dùng MongoDB nhưng vẫn cần Mongoose schema trong dự án production?”
   - **Ý cần đánh giá:** Hiểu trade-off giữa linh hoạt và kỷ luật dữ liệu.
   - **Hướng trả lời kỳ vọng:** Nêu schema giúp validation, chuẩn field, giảm dữ liệu bẩn và tăng tính ổn định API.

2. **Câu hỏi phỏng vấn:**  
   “`timestamps: true` có giá trị gì khi phân tích lỗi hoặc audit dữ liệu?”
   - **Ý cần đánh giá:** Tư duy observability và điều tra sự cố.
   - **Hướng trả lời kỳ vọng:** Dùng `createdAt/updatedAt` để truy vết lịch sử thay đổi, xác định bản ghi stale hoặc cập nhật bất thường.

3. **Câu hỏi phỏng vấn:**  
   “Khi nào nên lưu danh sách dưới dạng embedded array trong document, khi nào nên tách collection?”
   - **Ý cần đánh giá:** Khả năng thiết kế data model MongoDB theo access pattern.
   - **Hướng trả lời kỳ vọng:** Embed khi đọc cùng nhau, kích thước vừa phải; tách collection khi dữ liệu tăng lớn hoặc cần truy vấn độc lập nhiều chiều.

  ```bash
  git pull origin main
  ```
- **3. Start MongoDB:** Run the MongoDB container:
  ```bash
  docker compose -f .docker/mongodb.yaml up --build -d
  ```
- **4. Install dependencies and run the app:** Install packages and start the server:
  ```bash
  npm install
  npm run start:dev
  ```
- **5. Success signal:** The app runs on port `3000`; newly created documents include `createdAt` and `updatedAt`.

### Application Testing

- **Step 1:** Create a cat document with flexible metadata.

  **API Title:** **Cats API - create document - POST http://localhost:3000/cats**

  **How to call API:** Use Postman to send a `POST` request to `http://localhost:3000/cats`.

  **Body JSON:**
  ```json
  {
    "name": "Tom",
    "age": 3,
    "metadata": { "color": "orange", "weight": 4.5 },
    "hobbies": ["sleeping", "playing"]
  }
  ```

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/cats \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"name":"Tom","age":3,"metadata":{"color":"orange","weight":4.5},"hobbies":["sleeping","playing"]}'
  ```

- **Step 2:** Update a document by id and observe how `updatedAt` changes.

  **API Title:** **Cats API - patch cat age - PATCH http://localhost:3000/cats/{id}**

  **How to call API:** Use Postman to send a `PATCH` request to `http://localhost:3000/cats/{id}`.

  **Body JSON:**
  ```json
  {
    "age": 4
  }
  ```

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl -X PATCH http://localhost:3000/cats/REPLACE_ID \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"age":4}'
  ```

  **Trace code execution (by file):**
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts:21`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/mongoose-and-mongodb/src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts#L21) -> `CatsController.create()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:18`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/mongoose-and-mongodb/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L18) -> `CatsService.create()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/schemas/cat.schema.ts:9`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/mongoose-and-mongodb/src/modules/cats/schemas/cat.schema.ts#L9) -> `CatSchema` (`required`, `index`, `timestamps`)
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:41`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/mongoose-and-mongodb/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L41) -> `CatsService.update()`

  *Expected result:* Data is stored as flexible documents while validation enforces minimum consistency for critical fields.

## III. Core Concepts

### 1. ***Schema Discipline***

- **Role:** Mongoose schemas define a minimum data contract before documents are written.
- **Common mistake:** Assuming NoSQL means skipping validation entirely.
- **Production impact:** Inconsistent structures make querying and migration difficult.

### 2. ***MongoDB Indexing***

- **Role:** Indexes speed up queries on frequently filtered fields.
- **Common mistake:** Skipping indexes on hot fields like `name`, `email`, or `slug`.
- **Production impact:** Full collection scans and high latency at scale.

### 3. ***Flexible Fields***

- **Role:** `Object` and `Array` fields support flexible metadata/hobby storage without frequent migrations.
- **Common mistake:** Overusing free-form fields without an API contract.
- **Production impact:** Frontend/backend expectation mismatches and serialization bugs.

### 4. ***Query API and `.exec()`***

- **Role:** `.exec()` returns explicit Promises, making async flow and error handling clearer.
- **Common mistake:** Mixing callbacks, query objects, and `await` inconsistently.
- **Production impact:** Unpredictable error flow and difficult runtime tracing.

## IV. Advanced Techniques

For larger systems, combine schema validation with stronger patterns: add compound indexes for common filter/sort combinations, use partial indexes for sparse fields, and define DTO-level contracts that align with flexible document fields. This keeps read performance predictable while preserving MongoDB agility.

**Conclusion:** MongoDB is powerful not because it ignores schema, but because it allows flexible storage while Mongoose enforces discipline at the application boundary.

## V. Interview Questions

1. **Interview Question:**  
   "Why use Mongoose schemas in production even when using MongoDB?"
   - **What is being assessed:** Understanding the trade-off between flexibility and data discipline.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Explain that schemas enforce validation, standardize fields, reduce dirty data, and stabilize API behavior.

2. **Interview Question:**  
   "What value does `timestamps: true` provide in debugging and data auditing?"
   - **What is being assessed:** Observability and incident analysis mindset.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Use `createdAt/updatedAt` to trace changes, detect stale records, and investigate abnormal updates.

3. **Interview Question:**  
   "When should you store a list as an embedded array versus a separate collection?"
   - **What is being assessed:** MongoDB data modeling by access pattern.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Embed when data is read together and bounded in size; split when growth or independent querying becomes significant.

steps.title: Initialize the project and configure MongoDB
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Create a new project using NestJS CLI:
    ```bash
    nest new mongoose-and-mongodb-easy
    ```
  - Step 2: Navigate to the project directory:
    ```bash
    cd mongoose-and-mongodb-easy
    ```
  - Step 3: Install the required dependencies:
    ```bash
    npm install @nestjs/mongoose mongoose
    ```
  - Step 4: Create a `docker-compose.yml` file at the project root to start MongoDB:
    ```yaml
    services:
      mongo:
        image: mongo:7
        environment:
          MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME: mongo
          MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD: mongo
        ports:
          - "27017:27017"
    ```
  - Step 5: Start MongoDB:
    ```bash
    docker compose up -d
    ```
  - Step 6: Configure `MongooseModule.forRoot()` in `AppModule` with the connection string `mongodb://mongo:mongo@localhost:27017/blog?authSource=admin`.
- **Expected result:** MongoDB runs in Docker, NestJS application connects successfully to the `blog` database.
- **Conclusion:** The development environment is ready with MongoDB and Mongoose integrated into NestJS.

steps.title: Define Schema and Model
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Create `post.schema.ts`, define `PostSchema` using the decorator `@Schema({ timestamps: true })` to automatically add `createdAt` and `updatedAt`.
  - Step 2: Add fields with the `@Prop()` decorator:
    - `title`: type `string`, `required: true`, `index: true` to optimize queries by title.
    - `content`: type `string`, `required: true`.
    - `author`: type `string`, `required: true`.
    - `tags`: type `[String]`, default is an empty array `[]`.
    - `metadata`: type `Object` (Schema.Types.Mixed), allows storing flexible data without a fixed schema.
  - Step 3: Export the Schema using `SchemaFactory.createForClass(Post)`.
  - Step 4: Register the Schema in the module using `MongooseModule.forFeature([{ name: Post.name, schema: PostSchema }])`.
- **Expected result:** The `Post` Schema is correctly defined with automatic timestamps, an index on the `title` field, and a flexible `metadata` field.
- **Conclusion:** Mongoose Schema allows declaring a clear document structure while maintaining MongoDB's flexibility through the Mixed type field.

  - Bước 2: Thêm các trường với decorator `@Prop()`:
    - `title`: kiểu `string`, `required: true`, `index: true` để tối ưu truy vấn theo tiêu đề.
    - `content`: kiểu `string`, `required: true`.
    - `author`: kiểu `string`, `required: true`.
    - `tags`: kiểu `[String]`, mặc định là mảng rỗng `[]`.
    - `metadata`: kiểu `Object` (Schema.Types.Mixed), cho phép lưu trữ dữ liệu linh hoạt không cố định schema.
  - Bước 3: Export Schema bằng `SchemaFactory.createForClass(Post)`.
  - Bước 4: Đăng ký Schema trong module bằng `MongooseModule.forFeature([{ name: Post.name, schema: PostSchema }])`.
- **Kết quả mong đợi:** Schema `Post` được định nghĩa đúng cách với timestamps tự động, index trên trường `title`, và trường `metadata` linh hoạt.
- **Kết luận:** Mongoose Schema cho phép khai báo cấu trúc document rõ ràng trong khi vẫn giữ được tính linh hoạt của MongoDB thông qua trường Mixed type.

steps.title: Build Service and Controller
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Create `PostService` and inject the Model using `@InjectModel(Post.name) private postModel: Model<Post>`.
  - Step 2: Implement the `create(data)` method using `this.postModel.create(data)` to create a new document.
  - Step 3: Implement the `findAll()` method using `this.postModel.find().sort({ createdAt: -1 }).exec()` to return the post list sorted by creation time descending.
  - Step 4: Implement the `findOne(id)` method using `this.postModel.findById(id).exec()`. If not found, throw `NotFoundException`.
  - Step 5: Implement the `update(id, data)` method using `this.postModel.findByIdAndUpdate(id, data, { new: true }).exec()`. If not found, throw `NotFoundException`.
  - Step 6: Create `PostController` with 4 endpoints:
    - `POST /posts` accepts a body and calls `postService.create(body)`.
    - `GET /posts` calls `postService.findAll()`.
    - `GET /posts/:id` calls `postService.findOne(id)`.
    - `PATCH /posts/:id` accepts a body and calls `postService.update(id, body)`.
- **Expected result:** All 4 endpoints work correctly, supporting creation, list query, detail query, and post update.
- **Conclusion:** Service and Controller have been fully implemented with basic CRUD using Mongoose, correctly utilizing Model query methods.

steps.title: Test the endpoints
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Start the application:
    ```bash
    npm run start:dev
    ```
  - Step 2: Create a new post with tags and flexible metadata:
    ```bash
    curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/posts \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{
        "title": "Getting Started with MongoDB",
        "content": "MongoDB is a document database...",
        "author": "Jane Doe",
        "tags": ["mongodb", "nosql", "tutorial"],
        "metadata": { "readTime": 5, "featured": true, "source": "internal" }
      }'
    ```
  - Step 3: Create a second post with differently structured metadata:
    ```bash
    curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/posts \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{
        "title": "Mongoose Best Practices",
        "content": "Schema design is crucial...",
        "author": "Jane Doe",
        "tags": ["mongoose", "best-practices"],
        "metadata": { "series": "MongoDB Mastery", "part": 2 }
      }'
    ```
  - Step 4: Get the list of posts (verify sorted by createdAt descending):
    ```bash
    curl http://localhost:3000/posts
    ```
  - Step 5: Update a post, adding a new tag:
    ```bash
    curl -X PATCH http://localhost:3000/posts/<id> \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{
        "tags": ["mongodb", "nosql", "tutorial", "beginner"]
      }'
    ```
- **Expected result:**
  - `POST /posts` returns the new document with auto-generated `_id`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`.
  - `GET /posts` returns the post list with the newest post first.
  - `PATCH /posts/:id` returns the updated document with the `updatedAt` field changed.
  - Two posts have differently structured `metadata` fields but both save successfully, demonstrating MongoDB's flexibility.
- **Conclusion:** The Blog API works correctly with Mongoose and MongoDB, demonstrating flexible data storage through the Mixed type field and variable-length tags array.

    ```bash
        "tags": ["mongodb", "nosql", "tutorial", "beginner"]
      }'
    ```
- **Expected result:**
  - `POST /posts` returns the new document with auto-generated `_id`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`.
  - `GET /posts` returns the post list with the newest post first.
  - `PATCH /posts/:id` returns the updated document with the `updatedAt` field changed.
  - Two posts have differently structured `metadata` fields but both save successfully, demonstrating MongoDB's flexibility.
- **Conclusion:** The Blog API works correctly with Mongoose and MongoDB, demonstrating flexible data storage through the Mixed type field and variable-length tags array.

contents.title: Accelerating Systems with Redis Caching
contents.description: Learn how to integrate Redis into NestJS and apply caching at three layers: response layer, logic layer, and database query layer to reduce database load and improve response speed.
contents.body:
## I. Introduction

Both **PostgreSQL** and **MongoDB** persist data on disk (SSD/HDD). Even with indexing and optimized queries, complex operations still involve disk I/O, which is much slower than RAM.

Imagine **one million** concurrent users requesting the same leaderboard. If every request recomputes the result from scratch, the database becomes overloaded quickly. The practical solution is to introduce a **cache layer** between the application and database so frequently requested data does not need to be recomputed on every call.

## II. Essence

This lesson follows a **source-first** approach: read the code that applies cache at three layers, then call the same APIs repeatedly to observe cache misses, cache hits, and how Redis relieves PostgreSQL pressure.

Clone [here](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/tree/main/fullstack-mastery/caching-with-redis)

### Runtime Dependency Diagram

```mermaid
graph LR
    Client((Client))
    Client --> CatsController[CatsController]
    CatsController --> RespCache[CacheInterceptor - response layer]
    CatsController --> CatsService[CatsService]
    CatsService --> LogicCache[CACHE_MANAGER - logic layer]
    CatsService --> TypeOrmCache[TypeORM query cache - db layer]
    LogicCache --> Redis[(Redis)]
    TypeOrmCache --> Redis
    CatsService --> PG[(PostgreSQL)]
```

### Source Code Tree (file-level)

```mermaid
treeView-beta
    "src"
        "app.module.ts"
        "modules"
            "cats"
                "cats.module.ts"
                "cats.controller.ts"
                "cats.service.ts"
                "entities/cat.entity.ts"
        "infrastructure"
            "cache/cache.module.ts"
            "database/typeorm.config.ts"
```

### Environment Setup and Run Flow

- **1. Prerequisites:** `Node.js LTS`, `npm`, Docker Desktop, and Git are required.
- **2. Clone the demo source:** Clone/pull the source for consistent context:
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources.git
  cd resources/fullstack-mastery/caching-with-redis
  git pull origin main
  ```
- **3. Start PostgreSQL and Redis:** Run both data infrastructure services:
  ```bash
  docker compose -f .docker/postgresql.yaml up -d
  docker compose -f .docker/redis.yaml up -d
  ```
- **4. Install dependencies and run the app:** Install packages and start the server:
  ```bash
  npm install --legacy-peer-deps
  npm run start:dev
  ```
- **5. Success signal:** The app runs on port `3000`; repeated requests to the same endpoint become noticeably faster.

### Application Testing

- **Step 1:** Test response-layer caching by calling the same endpoint repeatedly.

  **API Title:** **Cats API - response layer cache - GET http://localhost:3000/cats/response-layer**

  **How to call API:** Use Postman to send `GET http://localhost:3000/cats/response-layer` twice in a row.

  **Body JSON:** No request body for `GET`.

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl http://localhost:3000/cats/response-layer
  curl http://localhost:3000/cats/response-layer
  ```

- **Step 2:** Test logic-layer and db-layer caching to compare control granularity.

  **API Title:** **Cats API - logic and db layer cache - GET http://localhost:3000/cats/logic-layer + GET http://localhost:3000/cats/db-layer**

  **How to call API:** Use Postman to call `GET /cats/logic-layer` and `GET /cats/db-layer`; call each endpoint twice.

  **Body JSON:** No request body for `GET`.

  Or use **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl http://localhost:3000/cats/logic-layer
  curl http://localhost:3000/cats/logic-layer
  curl http://localhost:3000/cats/db-layer
  curl http://localhost:3000/cats/db-layer
  ```

  **Trace code execution (by file):**
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts:18`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/caching-with-redis/src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts#L18) -> `CatsController.getResponseLayerCached()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts:27`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/caching-with-redis/src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts#L27) -> `CatsController.getLogicLayerCached()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:22`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/caching-with-redis/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L22) -> `CatsService.findWithLogicCache()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:48`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/caching-with-redis/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L48) -> `CatsService.findWithDatabaseCache()`
  - [`src/infrastructure/database/typeorm.config.ts:15`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/caching-with-redis/src/infrastructure/database/typeorm.config.ts#L15) -> query cache configuration

  *Expected result:* The first call is a cache miss and hits the DB; subsequent calls are cache hits and return faster.

## III. Core Concepts

### 1. ***Response-layer Caching***

- **Role:** Cache the entire controller response for fast rollout on read-heavy endpoints.
- **Common mistake:** Applying cache to highly volatile data without shortening TTL.
- **Production impact:** Users receive stale data for too long.

### 2. ***Logic-layer Caching***

- **Role:** Use `CACHE_MANAGER` for fine-grained key/TTL/invalidation control tied to business rules.
- **Common mistake:** Poor key namespacing that causes cache collisions across contexts.
- **Production impact:** Wrong data returned for specific users/tenants.

### 3. ***Database Query Caching***

- **Role:** TypeORM cache reduces repeated expensive queries without major business-code changes.
- **Common mistake:** Enabling query cache for strictly real-time transactional data.
- **Production impact:** Reports and metrics drift from freshly written records.

### 4. ***Cache Invalidation***

- **Role:** TTL or event-driven invalidation balances speed and freshness.
- **Common mistake:** Adding cache without a clear invalidation strategy.
- **Production impact:** Business bugs caused by prolonged stale data.

## IV. Advanced Techniques

In production, define a layered cache strategy instead of a one-size-fits-all TTL. Use short TTLs at response layer, explicit key invalidation at logic layer, and carefully scoped query cache at database layer. Track cache hit ratio, memory pressure, and stale-data incidents to continuously tune behavior.

**Conclusion:** Caching is not just "adding Redis"; it is deciding what to cache, where to cache it, and when to invalidate it safely.

## V. Interview Questions

1. **Interview Question:**  
   "Would you choose response-layer or logic-layer cache for a leaderboard that updates every 5 minutes?"
   - **What is being assessed:** Ability to choose cache layer based on data volatility and control needs.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Start with short-TTL response-layer cache; move to logic-layer cache if event-driven invalidation is needed.

2. **Interview Question:**  
   "What signals indicate your cache is hurting the system instead of helping?"
   - **What is being assessed:** Operational observation skills for stale/inconsistent data.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Mention DB mismatch, low hit ratio, key explosion, memory pressure, and invalidation failures.

3. **Interview Question:**  
   "How would you design cache keys for a multi-tenant system to prevent data leaks?"
   - **What is being assessed:** Safe namespace/key strategy design.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Include tenant/user scope in keys, use versioned prefixes, define TTL policy, and support tenant-scoped invalidation.

translations.value: Tăng tốc hệ thống với bộ nhớ đệm Redis
Tìm hiểu cách tích hợp Redis vào NestJS để caching dữ liệu ở 3 tầng khác nhau: Response layer, Logic layer và Database Query layer, từ đó giảm tải cho database và tăng tốc độ phản hồi.

## I. Lời mở đầu

Cả **PostgreSQL** lẫn **MongoDB** đều lưu trữ dữ liệu trên ổ cứng (SSD/HDD). Dù đã tối ưu bằng indexing hay aggregation, mọi truy vấn phức tạp vẫn phải thực hiện thao tác **I/O ổ cứng** — với tốc độ chậm hơn RAM hàng trăm lần.

Hãy tưởng tượng có **1 triệu** người dùng đồng thời truy cập để xem bảng xếp hạng "Top 10 Phim hay nhất". Nếu mọi request đều buộc database tính toán lại từ đầu — quét bảng, **GROUP BY**, sắp xếp — server sẽ quá tải và sụp đổ trong vài phút. Giải pháp là đặt một lớp **bộ nhớ đệm (Cache)** giữa ứng dụng và database, để những dữ liệu được truy vấn thường xuyên không cần phải tính toán lại mỗi lần.

## II. Bản chất

Bài này đi theo hướng **source-first**: đọc code áp dụng cache ở 3 tầng trước, rồi gọi API lặp lại để thấy rõ cache miss/hit và cách Redis giảm tải cho PostgreSQL.

Clone tại [đây](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/tree/main/fullstack-mastery/caching-with-redis)

### Sơ đồ phụ thuộc runtime

```mermaid
graph LR
    Client((Client))
    Client --> CatsController[CatsController]
    CatsController --> RespCache[CacheInterceptor - response layer]
    CatsController --> CatsService[CatsService]
    CatsService --> LogicCache[CACHE_MANAGER - logic layer]
    CatsService --> TypeOrmCache[TypeORM query cache - db layer]
    LogicCache --> Redis[(Redis)]
    TypeOrmCache --> Redis
    CatsService --> PG[(PostgreSQL)]
```

### Sơ đồ cây source code (file-level)

```mermaid
treeView-beta
    "src"
        "app.module.ts"
        "modules"
            "cats"
                "cats.module.ts"
                "cats.controller.ts"
                "cats.service.ts"
                "entities/cat.entity.ts"
        "infrastructure"
            "cache/cache.module.ts"
            "database/typeorm.config.ts"
```

### Chuẩn bị Môi trường và Luồng Cài đặt

- **1. Prerequisites:** Cần `Node.js LTS`, `npm`, Docker Desktop và git.
- **2. Clone source demo:** Clone/pull source để đọc đúng context code:
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources.git
  cd resources/fullstack-mastery/caching-with-redis
  git pull origin main
  ```
- **3. Khởi động PostgreSQL và Redis:** Chạy hai hạ tầng dữ liệu:
  ```bash
  docker compose -f .docker/postgresql.yaml up -d
  docker compose -f .docker/redis.yaml up -d
  ```
- **4. Cài dependency và chạy app:** Cài package rồi khởi động server:
  ```bash
  npm install --legacy-peer-deps
  npm run start:dev
  ```
- **5. Tín hiệu thành công:** App chạy cổng `3000`; gọi cùng endpoint lần 2 thấy thời gian phản hồi giảm rõ.

### Kiểm thử ứng dụng

- **Bước 1:** Test response-layer cache bằng cách gọi lặp endpoint giống nhau.

  **Tiêu đề API:** **Cats API - response layer cache - GET http://localhost:3000/cats/response-layer**

  **Hướng dẫn gọi API:** Dùng Postman gửi `GET` tới `http://localhost:3000/cats/response-layer` hai lần liên tiếp.

  **Body JSON:** Không có body với request `GET`.

  Hoặc dùng **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl http://localhost:3000/cats/response-layer
  curl http://localhost:3000/cats/response-layer
  ```

- **Bước 2:** Test logic-layer và db-layer cache để so sánh mức độ kiểm soát.

  **Tiêu đề API:** **Cats API - logic and db layer cache - GET http://localhost:3000/cats/logic-layer + GET http://localhost:3000/cats/db-layer**

  **Hướng dẫn gọi API:** Dùng Postman gọi lần lượt `GET /cats/logic-layer` và `GET /cats/db-layer`, mỗi endpoint gọi 2 lần.

  **Body JSON:** Không có body với request `GET`.

  Hoặc dùng **curl** (WSL2 / Bash / macOS):
  ```bash
  curl http://localhost:3000/cats/logic-layer
  curl http://localhost:3000/cats/logic-layer
  curl http://localhost:3000/cats/db-layer
  curl http://localhost:3000/cats/db-layer
  ```

  **Trace code execution (theo file):**
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts:18`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/caching-with-redis/src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts#L18) -> `CatsController.getResponseLayerCached()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts:27`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/caching-with-redis/src/modules/cats/cats.controller.ts#L27) -> `CatsController.getLogicLayerCached()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:22`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/caching-with-redis/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L22) -> `CatsService.findWithLogicCache()`
  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:48`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/caching-with-redis/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L48) -> `CatsService.findWithDatabaseCache()`
  - [`src/infrastructure/database/typeorm.config.ts:15`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/caching-with-redis/src/infrastructure/database/typeorm.config.ts#L15) -> query cache configuration

  *Kết quả mong đợi:* Lần gọi đầu cache miss sẽ truy vấn DB; lần gọi sau cache hit trả dữ liệu nhanh hơn.

  *Kết luận:* Redis giúp hạ áp lực database, nhưng cần chiến lược invalidation để tránh stale data.

## III. Các khái niệm cốt lõi

### 1. ***Response-layer caching***

- **Vai trò:** Cache toàn bộ response ở tầng controller, triển khai nhanh cho endpoint read-heavy.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Áp cache cho endpoint dữ liệu biến động cao mà không giảm TTL.
- **Hậu quả production:** Người dùng nhận stale data quá lâu.

### 2. ***Logic-layer caching***

- **Vai trò:** Dùng `CACHE_MANAGER` để kiểm soát key/TTL/invalidation chi tiết theo nghiệp vụ.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Đặt key không có namespace rõ ràng dẫn tới đè cache giữa các context.
- **Hậu quả production:** Trả sai dữ liệu theo user/tenant.

### 3. ***Database query caching***

- **Vai trò:** TypeORM cache giảm tải query lặp nặng mà không đổi nhiều business code.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Bật cache query cho dữ liệu transactional cần realtime tuyệt đối.
- **Hậu quả production:** Báo cáo/metrics lệch so với dữ liệu mới ghi.

### 4. ***Cache invalidation***

- **Vai trò:** TTL hoặc event-driven invalidation giúp cân bằng tốc độ và độ tươi dữ liệu.
- **Lỗi thường gặp:** Chỉ cache mà không có chiến lược xóa cache khi dữ liệu đổi.
- **Hậu quả production:** Tăng bug nghiệp vụ do dữ liệu cũ kéo dài.

## IV. Kết luận

**Redis** là công cụ không thể thiếu trong kiến trúc Backend hiện đại. Với 3 tầng caching — **Response**, **Logic** và **Database Query** — NestJS mang lại sự linh hoạt tối đa trong việc lựa chọn chiến lược cache phù hợp với từng trường hợp sử dụng cụ thể.

**Kết luận:** Caching không chỉ là "thêm Redis vào hệ thống" — mà là hiểu rõ dữ liệu nào cần cache, cache ở tầng nào, và khi nào cần vô hiệu hóa cache để đảm bảo người dùng luôn nhận được dữ liệu chính xác.

## V. Các mẫu câu phỏng vấn

1. **Câu hỏi phỏng vấn:**  
   “Bạn chọn response-layer hay logic-layer cache cho endpoint bảng xếp hạng cập nhật mỗi 5 phút?”
   - **Ý cần đánh giá:** Năng lực chọn tầng cache theo tốc độ thay đổi dữ liệu và độ linh hoạt nghiệp vụ.
   - **Hướng trả lời kỳ vọng:** Có thể bắt đầu response-layer với TTL ngắn; chuyển logic-layer nếu cần invalidation chủ động theo sự kiện.

2. **Câu hỏi phỏng vấn:**  
   “Dấu hiệu nào cho thấy cache đang gây hại thay vì giúp hệ thống?”
   - **Ý cần đánh giá:** Tư duy quan sát hệ thống và phát hiện stale/inconsistent data.
   - **Hướng trả lời kỳ vọng:** Nêu các dấu hiệu như dữ liệu lệch DB, hit ratio thấp, key bùng nổ, memory pressure, invalidation thất bại.

3. **Câu hỏi phỏng vấn:**  
   “Bạn thiết kế cache key thế nào cho hệ thống multi-tenant để không leak dữ liệu?”
   - **Ý cần đánh giá:** Khả năng thiết kế namespace/key strategy an toàn.
   - **Hướng trả lời kỳ vọng:** Thêm tenantId/user scope vào key, chuẩn prefix version, kiểm soát TTL và xóa key theo tenant khi có cập nhật lớn.

  - [`src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts:22`](https://github.com/StarCi-Academy/resources/blob/main/fullstack-mastery/caching-with-redis/src/modules/cats/cats.service.ts#L22) -> `CatsService.findWithLogicCache()`

  *Expected result:* The first call is a cache miss and hits the DB; subsequent calls are cache hits and return faster.

## III. Core Concepts

### 1. ***Response-layer Caching***

- **Role:** Cache the entire controller response for fast rollout on read-heavy endpoints.
- **Common mistake:** Applying cache to highly volatile data without shortening TTL.
- **Production impact:** Users receive stale data for too long.

### 2. ***Logic-layer Caching***

- **Role:** Use `CACHE_MANAGER` for fine-grained key/TTL/invalidation control tied to business rules.
- **Common mistake:** Poor key namespacing that causes cache collisions across contexts.
- **Production impact:** Wrong data returned for specific users/tenants.

### 3. ***Database Query Caching***

- **Role:** TypeORM cache reduces repeated expensive queries without major business-code changes.
- **Common mistake:** Enabling query cache for strictly real-time transactional data.
- **Production impact:** Reports and metrics drift from freshly written records.

### 4. ***Cache Invalidation***

- **Role:** TTL or event-driven invalidation balances speed and freshness.
- **Common mistake:** Adding cache without a clear invalidation strategy.
- **Production impact:** Business bugs caused by prolonged stale data.

## IV. Advanced Techniques

In production, define a layered cache strategy instead of a one-size-fits-all TTL. Use short TTLs at response layer, explicit key invalidation at logic layer, and carefully scoped query cache at database layer. Track cache hit ratio, memory pressure, and stale-data incidents to continuously tune behavior.

**Conclusion:** Caching is not just "adding Redis"; it is deciding what to cache, where to cache it, and when to invalidate it safely.

## V. Interview Questions

1. **Interview Question:**  
   "Would you choose response-layer or logic-layer cache for a leaderboard that updates every 5 minutes?"
   - **What is being assessed:** Ability to choose cache layer based on data volatility and control needs.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Start with short-TTL response-layer cache; move to logic-layer cache if event-driven invalidation is needed.

2. **Interview Question:**  
   "What signals indicate your cache is hurting the system instead of helping?"
   - **What is being assessed:** Operational observation skills for stale/inconsistent data.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Mention DB mismatch, low hit ratio, key explosion, memory pressure, and invalidation failures.

3. **Interview Question:**  
   "How would you design cache keys for a multi-tenant system to prevent data leaks?"
   - **What is being assessed:** Safe namespace/key strategy design.
   - **Expected answer direction:** Include tenant/user scope in keys, use versioned prefixes, define TTL policy, and support tenant-scoped invalidation.

steps.title: Initialize the project and configure Redis
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Create a new project using NestJS CLI:
    ```bash
    nest new caching-with-redis-easy
    ```
  - Step 2: Navigate to the project directory:
    ```bash
    cd caching-with-redis-easy
    ```
  - Step 3: Install the required dependencies:
    ```bash
    npm install @nestjs/cache-manager cache-manager cache-manager-redis-store redis
    ```
  - Step 4: Create a `docker-compose.yml` file at the project root to start Redis:
    ```yaml
    services:
      redis:
        image: redis:7-alpine
        ports:
          - "6379:6379"
    ```
  - Step 5: Start Redis:
    ```bash
    docker compose up -d
    ```
  - Step 6: Configure `CacheModule.register()` in `AppModule` with `store` as `redisStore`, `host: 'localhost'`, `port: 6379`, and `ttl: 60` (seconds).
- **Expected result:** Redis runs in Docker, NestJS application connects successfully to the Redis server.
- **Conclusion:** The development environment is ready with Redis and Cache Manager integrated into NestJS.

steps.title: Create ProductModule with in-memory data
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Create `ProductModule`, `ProductService`, `ProductController`.
  - Step 2: In `ProductService`, initialize a sample data array:
    ```typescript
    private products = [
      { id: 1, name: 'Laptop', price: 999 },
      { id: 2, name: 'Phone', price: 699 },
      { id: 3, name: 'Tablet', price: 499 },
    ];
    ```
  - Step 3: Implement the `findAll()` method returning the entire products array.
  - Step 4: Implement the `create(data)` method adding a new product to the array with an auto-incrementing id.
  - Step 5: In `ProductController`, create endpoint `GET /products` calling `findAll()` and `POST /products` calling `create(body)`.
- **Expected result:** Both endpoints work correctly with in-memory data, without caching yet.
- **Conclusion:** The core business module is ready; the next step will add the caching layer with Redis.

steps.title: Integrate Cache Manager into Service
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Inject `CACHE_MANAGER` into `ProductService` using `@Inject(CACHE_MANAGER) private cacheManager: Cache`.
  - Step 2: Update the `findAll()` method with caching logic:
    - Check cache first: `const cached = await this.cacheManager.get('products')`.
    - If cache exists, return the cached data immediately.
    - If no cache, get data from the in-memory array, save to cache using `await this.cacheManager.set('products', this.products, 60)`, then return the data.
  - Step 3: Add console logs to distinguish responses from cache vs data source:
    - When serving from cache: `console.log('Serving from cache')`.
    - When serving from data source: `console.log('Serving from data source')`.
  - Step 4: Update the `create(data)` method: after adding the new product, delete the cache using `await this.cacheManager.del('products')` to ensure the next `GET /products` call fetches the latest data.
- **Expected result:** The first `GET /products` call fetches from the data source and saves to cache. The second call returns from cache. After `POST /products`, cache is deleted and the next `GET /products` call fetches from the data source again.
- **Conclusion:** Proper cache invalidation ensures data consistency between cache and data source.

    - Nếu có cache, trả về dữ liệu từ cache ngay lập tức.

steps.title: Test the caching flow
steps.body:
- **Steps to follow:**
  - Step 1: Start the application:
    ```bash
    npm run start:dev
    ```
  - Step 2: Call `GET /products` for the first time:
    ```bash
    curl http://localhost:3000/products
    ```
    Check the terminal log shows `Serving from data source`.
  - Step 3: Call `GET /products` a second time immediately:
    ```bash
    curl http://localhost:3000/products
    ```
    Check the terminal log shows `Serving from cache`.
  - Step 4: Create a new product (trigger cache invalidation):
    ```bash
    curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/products \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{ "name": "Monitor", "price": 399 }'
    ```
  - Step 5: Call `GET /products` again:
    ```bash
    curl http://localhost:3000/products
    ```
    Check the terminal log shows `Serving from data source` (cache was deleted). Verify the response includes the newly created product.
  - Step 6: Call `GET /products` once more to confirm cache has been recreated:
    ```bash
    curl http://localhost:3000/products
    ```
    Check the terminal log shows `Serving from cache`.
- **Expected result:**
  - Call 1: data source, response contains 3 initial products.
  - Call 2: cache, response same as call 1.
  - After `POST /products`: cache is deleted.
  - Call 3: data source, response contains 4 products (including the new product).
  - Call 4: cache, response same as call 3.
- **Conclusion:** The complete caching flow has been demonstrated: cache hits speed up responses, cache invalidation when data changes ensures consistency, and cache automatically recreates after being deleted.
